#1758. Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:

He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

Possession: Chelsea 50%-50% AC MilanShots: 18-5Shots on target: 8-0Corners: 7-2

The final whistle is blown in Jakarta and Chelsea have cruised to a 3-0 win over AC Milan. Goals from Caicedo and a double from Pedro either side of half-time have led Xabi Alonso’s side to the victory. They have one more game out in the Far East before returning home to the UK.

What a performance! 👏 pic.twitter.com/GcUZXwXbRj

Ramos is picked out after making a run into the Chelsea box and is denied by Sanchez. However, the offside flag has gone up anyway against Ramos. AC Milan have barely threatened the Chelsea goal in this second half.

A late change for Chelsea as Sarr replaces Fofana.

Chelsea are seeking their fourth goal as Quenda strikes a shot powerfully from just outside the box but it goes narrowly wide. Xabi Alonso’s side have dominated this second half.

Estevao has the chance to score moments after coming on after good work from the Brazilian down Chelsea’s right but is denied by a good save from Torriani.

Chelsea make a triple changes as Estevao, Mudryk and Watson come on. Mudryk made his return after his doping ban against Juventus during the week.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal once more. Jackson gets the better of Vladimirov down Chelsea’s left and moves into the AC Milan penalty area. Jackson opens up his body as if he is going to curl his shot into the far corner but instead shoots towards the near corner, with his effort coming off the post.

Ricci goes for an audacious strike with the outside of his right foot from outside the box but his effort misses the target.

Palmer was deep in conversation with his boss Alonso during that water break.

Chelsea made a substitution during that break as Anselmino comes on for Hato. Thus far, Chelsea have made three changes in this game and Alonso did confirm before the game that some players should be able to go the full 90 this far into pre-season.

Chelsea hit the post. Quenda receives the ball on the right side of the penalty area and quickly moves the ball onto his right foot. The 19-year-old then smashes a shot towards goal and the ball flies into the outside of the post. Quenda struck that with some venom.

Palmer has a chance to get Chelsea’s fourth from the left side of the box but AC Milan keeper Torriani makes the save down to his left.

AC Milan have offered very little going forward since the break and Sanchez has not been troubled in the Chelsea goal.

AC Milan have a good chance to get a goal back. Musah finds space on the right side of the box and cuts it back towards the penalty spot. He picks out Nkunku but the former Chelsea man wastes the opportunity.

Palestra is found with a cross from the right to the far post. Palestra takes a touch but his shot goes into the side netting.

Ruben Amorim is demanding a free-kick just outside the Chelsea box but the referee does not agree. Replays show that AC Milan probably should have been given the free-kick as it was a foul by Fofana on Ramos. Both players went down but are back to their feet.

Xabi Alonso is going to make his first two changes of the game as Jackson and Quenda replace Welbeck and Neto.

Chelsea have their third and their new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee will be delighted with that one. Lavia plays a flat delivery from a corner out on the left to Caicedo on the edge of the box. Caicedo hits it first time on the volley with the outside of his right foot and picks out the bottom right corner with perfection.

Chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

AC Milan have made a raft of changes at the break, which includes their new record signing Ramos, who has joined from PSG this summer. Former Chelsea man Nkunku is also on. Milan were back out from the dressing rooms a fair bit earlier than Chelsea were. It is rather farcical how long Chelsea took to re-emerge for the second half and they just saunter out as if nothing is up. Why on earth did the officials just allow Chelsea to take over 20 minutes for half-time?

Nearly 25 minutes after the first half concluded, we are finally back under way in Jakarta.

Possession: Chelsea 58%-42% AC MilanShots: 6-4Shots on target: 3-0Corners: 4-2

The first half in Jakarta is brought an end and Chelsea take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Pedro’s goal on the stroke of half-time.

90 seconds into added time at the end of this first half, we have the first goal in Jakarta. Caicedo’s delivery from the right picks out Pedro, who has a free header inside the six-yard box and makes no mistake, picking out the corner. Pedro really should not have been afforded so much space in the six-yard box.

Palestra makes a run in behind the AC Milan defence and is found but De Winter gets back to put it behind for a corner...

Due to the water break, there will be three additional minutes at the end of this first half.

The first booking of the game goes the way of AC Milan as Pavlovic clears out Palestra. A deserved booking.

Neto and Pedro exchange a good one-two down Chelsea’s right to put the former racing down the right wing. Neto then tries to find Welbeck in the centre of the box but it is just behind him.

Then, moments later, Pedro spurns a great chance for Chelsea. Palestra’s cross from the left is just out of Palmer’s reach but falls straight to Pedro, who blazes over from 12 yards out. He was leaning back and should really be hitting the target.

The space opens up for Palmer to take on a shot from range but his effort is blocked by De Winter. Palmer has not managed to have that much of an effect on this game thus far.

Pavlovic drives forward from his defensive position through the Chelsea half. He gets all the way to the Chelsea box before shooting but he looked to lack conviction, firing off target.

We will pause for a drinks break, which unfortunately we became accustomed to during the World Cup. Palmer takes the chance to take a seat on the bench whilst taking on some fluids.

Neto takes a first-time shot from outside the box and looks to curl it into the far corner, forcing Torriani into a decent save diving down to his right.

That is good one-vs-one defending from Achemapong. Estupinan plays the ball into the path of Leao, who drives through the Chelsea half down AC Milan’s left. As Leao approaches the Chelsea box, Leao attempts to push it past Acheampong but the young Chelsea defender times his sliding challenge to perfection and puts it behind for a corner. Sanchez punches it out to the edge of the box, where Comotto takes it on his chest before volleying towards goal. The ball goes behind for another corner, which Chelsea just about scramble away.

Chelsea hit the post. Palestra drives forward for Chelsea down their left before the ball falls to Welbeck on the left side of the box. Welbeck’s effort hits the outside of the post. AC Milan keeper Torriani appeared though to always have it covered.

Chelsea gift the ball away inside their own half and Leao drives forward. The Portuguese forward moves into the Chelsea penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is blocked.

A big, big chance for Chelsea to take the lead. A long ball is played forward in behind the AC Milan defence and Pedro gets the better of De Winter inside the Milan penalty area. It is then a one-on-one chance with Torriani but Pedro hits it straight at the Milan goalkeeper. Torriani should have come to claim that long ball and then Pedro should probably have buried that opportunity.

Chelsea win their third corner of the game as Palmer’s cross from the right takes a couple of deflections off AC Milan defender. Captain Caicedo has trotted over to take it out on the left. He sends it into a good area but a foul on the AC Milan keeper Torriani is given against Pedro.

Neto clips a free-kick into the AC Milan penalty area, which is chested down by Pedro. The Brazilian holds the ball up well inside the box before winning a corner. Chelsea play it short and Palmer crosses to the back post, where Palestra wins Chelsea another corner, this time out on the left.

Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

Palestra, who has joined Chelsea this summer from Atalanta, is proving his versatility today; he has mostly operated for Chelsea at right-back so far this pre-season but he is starting at left-back in this game.

Camarda is played in behind the Chelsea defence and tries to get the better of Fofana inside the Chelsea penalty area but the ball just runs out of play across the byline before Camarda can square the ball.

We are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

The atmosphere is building. 🇮🇩📈 pic.twitter.com/fhXfDVAf6s

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

#1757. Roma in Serie A title mix, says Gasperini after 3-0 win over Sassuolo

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Gian Piero Gasperini believes his Roma team are firmly in the mix for the Serie A title after they dispatched Sassuolo 3-0.

Roma bounced back from their capitulation against Manchester United by swatting aside Sassuolo at Stadio Olimpico on Saturday.

Mario Hermoso and Rodrigo Mora were on target for Roma, who also benefited from Sebastian Walukiewicz's own goal.

Roma posted 3.73 expected goals in a dominant performance, as they made it 18 home league games unbeaten, which is their longest such run under a single manager since a 22-game streak between January 2016 and February 2017 under Luciano Spalletti (W19 D3).

They also became only the fourth team in the last 65 years to score more than 30 goals after 11 Serie A matches in a season, following Juventus (33), Napoli (32) and Lazio (31), all of whom achieved this in 2017-18. Roma have netted 31 league goals already this season.

Roma moved up to second, at least temporarily, with Inter in action on Sunday. Lazio are top.

— AS Roma English (@ASRomaEN) November 7, 2026

And Gasperini feels his team can now be labelled as title challengers.

"It [is] an incredible run of games, we lost only to Real Madrid and Manchester United, but also had a run of victories, drew with Como and Napoli," Gasperini said.

"Those two defeats hurt because they were late and we were leading, but they did come at the end of strong performances and against top-level opponents.

"Undoubtedly, this season we improved a lot in attack, so now we score lots of goals in different ways and with different players. Even when we lost, we scored lots of goals.

"In fact, I don't believe this is a response to a defeat, it's just more confirmation from this team of the track they are on.

"It's fun to play this season. We must not delude ourselves or disappoint ourselves, so there's no harm in dreaming, especially with the journey that we are on. I don't know what we could be capable of achieving.

"Inter are the best placed to win. For the rest, all of us are in the mix, including us, and can have our chances."

Mora had already hit the crossbar before Hermoso put Roma ahead in the 27th minute, firing home after initially trying to set up Donyell Malen.

Walukiewicz inadvertently turned in from Malen's shot, and Roma grabbed their third in the second half when Mora picked out the bottom corner.

#1756. Tottenham get new red card review as Leeds defender escapes punishment

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Jayden Bogle should have been shown a red card during Leeds United’s win over Tottenham, says former Premier League referee Keith Hackett.

As Spurs’ three-game winning streak was snapped on Saturday afternoon, the biggest talking point came shortly before half-time when Mathys Tel was eventually forced off after being on the receiving end of a strong challenge from Jayden Bogle.

Replays showed the the Leeds defender had landed his studs on the Frenchman’s left Achilles, but - to the surprise of many - avoided any punishment from referee John Brooks.

In fact, VAR reviewed the challenge for around four minutes and ultimately deemed it did not meet the threshold for serious foul play.

Standard Sport understands Spurs are set to submit a formal complaint about the decision to not send off Bogle, writing to refereeing body, Pro Ref, for an explanation.

Meanwhile, upon reviewing the incident himself, Hackett believes the nature of the challenge should have resulted in a red card.

“This challenge should frankly always be red carded,” he said in a post on X, formerly Twitter.

“The Achilles is a very vulnerable area and the safety of the player must be taken into account.”

On the incident, though, Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi said he still had full confidence in VAR and insisted his side could not blame the officials for the result at Elland Road.

“No, I have big confidence in the referee,” De Zerbi said when asked if he would have wanted referee John Brooks to go to the monitor to look at Bogle’s challenge.

“Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR, and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know. But we have confidence, we have to keep our eyes on the performance where we can improve.”

#1755. Arsenal 'should have been awarded a penalty' as Mikel Arteta gets clarity after Hull win

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta has received some clarity over the offside law after Arsenal were denied a penalty in their win over Hull.

On a day of controversial refereeing decisions in the Premier League, the incident in question at the Emirates Stadium occurred in the first half when Kai Havertz was pulled to the ground inside the box.

The German’s appeals was initially ignored and play was allowed to continue before a sudden halt was called to allow referee Farai Hallam to go to the monitor and review the replay.

While Hallam announced that a foul had been committed by Hull defender Nobel Mendy, Arsenal were NOT awarded a penalty because Havertz was in an offside position.

Now, as the rules regarding such incidents are ambiguous, Arteta has called for clarity as one interpretation is that Havertz was not committing an offside offence due to not “attempting to play the ball or challenging an opponent for the ball”.

“I don’t know, I haven’t watched it back,” the Arsenal manager said in his post-match press conference.

“I didn’t watch it back so I don’t have to lie to you guys. I was surprised, because when they sent the referee to the monitor the bench was telling me that it’s a clear penalty, it’s pulling.

“I know they decided not to because the starting position of Kai was offside, so I don’t know what the interpretation is. I’m sure they will make that clear to understand it.”

Former Premier League referee chief Keith Hackett has attempted to clear up the situation by posting on X, formerly Twitter: “The Offside Law is clear and a penalty kick should have been awarded.”

Ultimately, the confusion over whether Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty was not made into a bigger talking point after the game as Martin Odegaard broke Hull’s resistance in the 72nd minute.

That result, coupled with Manchester City’s loss to Nottingham Forest, means the Gunners have a six-point lead at the Premier League summit.

#1754. Jurgen Klopp calls up Bayern Munich target Wael Mohya

By Naim Beneddra | 07 Nov 2026 12:06

Former Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp has handed a surprise Germany call-up to a 17-year-old Bundesliga prospect who is attracting interest from Bayern Munich, with his club facing a difficult battle to secure his long-term future.

Borussia Monchengladbach attacking midfielder Wael Mohya has been included in Germany's 24-man squad for their upcoming Nations League fixtures against Serbia and the Netherlands, earning his first senior international call-up following an impressive breakthrough at club level.

The teenager's emergence has been one of the few positives in a troubled campaign for Gladbach, who suffered another setback on Friday evening with a 3-1 defeat away to Hamburg.

That result has increased the pressure on Alexander Blessin's side, while Mohya's growing reputation is already attracting attention from several of Germany's leading clubs.

According to Sky Sport Germany, Bayern are monitoring the youngster alongside Borussia Dortmund, Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig, with Gladbach attempting to negotiate improved contractual terms.

Mohya's inclusion represents one of the most eye-catching decisions in Klopp's latest Germany squad, particularly given the attacking midfielder's limited experience at senior level.

The 17-year-old has progressed rapidly since becoming Borussia Monchengladbach's youngest-ever competitive debutant in October 2025, when he appeared against Karlsruher SC in the DFB-Pokal.

He subsequently made 17 senior appearances during the 2025-26 campaign, scoring twice and providing one assist.

Mohya has taken another step forward this season, establishing himself as a regular option under Blessin and producing some of Gladbach's most encouraging attacking performances.

His most notable contribution came on October 23, when he scored once and assisted another goal in a 3-2 victory over Stuttgart, securing Gladbach's first Bundesliga win of the campaign.

The youngster has registered two league goals and one assist this term, operating primarily from the left flank while using his close control and acceleration to move into central attacking positions.

He also became the fourth-youngest player in Bundesliga history to score in consecutive matches, having found the net against Hoffenheim and Stuttgart.

Klopp has now rewarded that progress with an opportunity to impress at international level.

Speaking about Mohya's selection, the Germany manager explained that the teenager's ability to compete regularly in the Bundesliga had already made him stand out.

"There aren't many 17-year-olds playing in the Bundesliga. That alone is an outstanding achievement. But he's doing well, too," Klopp said, as reported by Sport1.

The former Liverpool boss also stressed the importance of handling young players carefully rather than making premature promises about their international futures.

Klopp revealed that he had already held three conversations with Mohya and was particularly impressed by his confidence and maturity.

The German coach intends to assess the youngster in training during the international break, although his presence in the squad does not guarantee a debut.

Mohya could make his first senior appearance when Germany visit Serbia on November 13 or host the Netherlands three days later.

The call-up also represents an important development for a player of Moroccan descent who has previously represented Germany at youth level.

Mohya's international recognition comes at an awkward time for Gladbach, who are facing uncertainty over the future of one of their most promising academy graduates.

According to Sky Sport Germany, Bayern Munich, Dortmund, Leverkusen and Leipzig are all keeping a close eye on his progress.

The teenager remains under contract at Borussia-Park until June 2028, but Gladbach have already opened discussions over an improved agreement in an attempt to strengthen their position.

Reports suggest that the club are prepared to offer Mohya an annual salary package worth approximately €2m (£1.75m), potentially doubling his current earnings.

A release clause could also become part of the negotiations, although no agreement has been announced.

Crucially, Sky reports that Gladbach's chances of retaining the youngster may depend on their ability to preserve their Bundesliga status.

A January departure is currently considered unlikely, but the situation could change considerably when the summer transfer window opens.

Sporting director Rouven Schroder has acknowledged that keeping talented young players indefinitely is unrealistic, while maintaining that the club enjoys a positive relationship with Mohya and his representatives.

"We are in contact with him, his parents and his agency," Schroder explained during an appearance on Doppelpass.

Nevertheless, the sporting director also admitted that Mohya would not necessarily spend his entire career at Gladbach, recognising the financial realities facing clubs developing highly sought-after talent.

The youngster has strong personal connections to Borussia, having joined the academy as a child and grown up approximately 25 minutes from the club's stadium.

That relationship could prove important during contract negotiations, particularly with several Bundesliga rivals monitoring developments.

However, Gladbach's immediate problems remain on the pitch.

Friday's defeat at Hamburg saw the visitors reduced to 10 men shortly after half time, before conceding twice in the second period.

Mohya completed the match and nearly scored in the closing stages, curling an effort narrowly wide of the top corner.

For now, the midfielder's priority is an opportunity to impress Klopp on international duty.

Whether Gladbach can build a competitive enough team around him to secure his longer-term future remains a significant question ahead of next summer.

#1753. AC Milan 0-2 Ferencvaros: Five things we learned – a poor squad picked apart

AC Milan’s Europa League misery continued at San Siro on Thursday night as they were beaten 2-0 by Ferencvaros.

Ruben Amorim made six changes to the team that won the derby against Inter, hoping that the entire group would remain buoyed by that performance to secure a much-needed win in Europe. However, what followed was the worst performance of his tenure so far.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Lenny Joseph netted twice in the second half to capitalise on errors and fire the Hungarian side to a memorable win. Ferencvaros were not even rocked by a red card to the substitute Yusuf as they kept the Rossoneri at bay quite easily, securing a two-goal win they deserved.

The result means that Milan have now dropped out of even the top 24 spots, and they can just about say goodbye to any hopes of direct last-16 qualification barring a miracle. Ivan Stoev has five things we learned from another dismal midweek game.

It’s difficult to pick five talking points after a game like this, as we can probably spend quite a bit of time discussing how bad each of the players were. But let’s try to address the bigger issue.

This squad is full of sheep, lacking both leaders and the quality to compete. We can talk all about how much Amorim rotates the squad and try to ease the blow by suggesting the Rossoneri didn’t field their best XI. Yet, if the management were serious about making the club competitive, then the rotational players should be above the quality of almost all teams competing in the Europa League, bar a few.

Obviously, if we assume Amorim is the right choice and Gerry Cardinale is serious, then it will take a lot more than a single transfer window and three new players to get Milan to compete on a few fronts, which was further proven against Ferencvaros.

Out of the whole squad, the only player that can change a game is Diego Moreira, who doesn’t play every game and has lots of room for improvement still. Not to mention that playing with the likes of Filippo Terracciano, Ardon Jashari and even Goncalo Ramos is not helping Belgium at all.

The rest of the squad lack either the quality or the mentality. The collective arrogance on the pitch was insufferable to watch, with Ferencvaros looking like the only side that had any desire to actually win. Whilst the Diavolo looked like they were playing a game in the park with no aggression, no focus, no intensity. No nothing.

It’s a bit pointless to discuss individuals because I think the wider point is clear – Milan lack leaders, Milan lack quality and Milan lack a game changer that can get the ball and make something happen when the tough gets going.

It was made evident after four games in the Europa League and a few blunders in Serie A that there’s lots of work to be done in January and next summer.

Again, it’s difficult to pick and choose which player to discuss, but given Ramos is the Rossoneri’s most expensive signing ever, it’s probably fair that the pressure starts mounting on him.

Listen, I wasn’t too bothered by the lack of goals initially, as the striker did well in the build-up and opened up space for his teammates; he also ran a lot in both phases of the game. Let’s also be honest, he has lacked the service to actually get the goal-scoring opportunities.

Nevertheless, in the last few games and especially against Ferencvaros, he has been dire – his build-up is poor, his ball control is pretty bad and when he does get a shot off, it’s usually miles away.

Now, obviously he’s not a striker that’s going to create chances for himself; he lacks the pace and the trickery, which is fine if you are good in the other aspects of the game. However, we can’t keep grasping for straws.

The reality is that the former PSG man is just not living up to the expectations given the hefty sum paid for him in the summer.

In retrospect, maybe it wasn’t wise to spend such a sum on a player who needs quality around him in order to be a better facilitator or to receive more chances overall. The reality as of now is that the Portuguese is a disappointment.

Again, as we said, most players in the squad lack quality or mentality and unfortunately for us there are some that lack both and it’s way past the tipping point at this stage.

Terracciano, for starters, has not shown anything worth mentioning in all of his games with the red and black shirt and there’s really no reason for him to get minutes. Even without pressure, he’s just not of the needed level.

Jashari is another one that the fans and the management have hoped will bounce back after his lengthy injury after joining Milan. Yet, he’s probably had one good game from start to finish and there’s always gaps in his game.

It’s probably wise at this point to accept he’s not going to live up to the expectations and a solution needs to be found on the market, especially given Luka Modric will most likely be retiring at the end of the season.

There are also other players in this category that didn’t necessarily participate in last night’s game but should have the same fate – Pervis Estupinan and Ruben Loftus-Cheek to name a couple.

If nothing else, these poor performances should highlight to the management where the gap in quality is and what the strategy on the transfer market should be.

4. De Winter’s disastrous performance proves costly

I think the biggest individual call-out should definitely be the Belgian, who played an awful back pass to Lorenzo Torriani on the first goal. Yes, the keeper could’ve and should’ve done much better, but that back pass was just so sloppy – it could put an outfield player in a tricky situation, let alone a goalkeeper that perhaps isn’t as comfortable with his feet.

This especially coming from a player who should’ve been a certainty at the back given the heavily rotated squad.

We can also partly criticise the intervention on the second goal, because it started the whole sequence leading to the Joseph’s brace. Yes, it was a bit unlucky where the ball ended up, but you can also argue it was sloppy, the same way you can argue that a keeper clearing the ball into the opponent’s feet after a shot instead of towards the corner is the keeper’s fault to an extent.

It’s just unacceptable to go from bullying Thuram to being bullied by not even Ferencvaros’s first-choice striker.

5. Amorim’s tactics fail, but the players also struggle

I think it’s probably fair to criticise the Portuguese coach a bit too, as the Hungarians totally outplayed the Diavolo at the San Siro and were tactically better. All in all, they had the answer to everything Milan tried to offer on the night.

At the same time, I’m torn to put the blame fully on Ruben Amorim because he did make a triple change at half-time, bringing on Pulisic, Moreira and Gila, which was still at 0-0. At that point, the Rossoneri had more than enough quality on the pitch to be able to deal with whatever Ferencvaros had to offer.

Instead, two individual mistakes gave away the opening goal and it all went downhill from there. Even after the red card, Milan struggled to create a big chance.

I personally struggle to blame this fully on tactics given all the circumstances and we are back to the point that the Milan squad are just not good enough and lacks that killer mentality.

#1752. Manchester United XI vs Aston Villa: Predicted lineup, confirmed team news, injury latest for Premier League today

Manchester United are without Carlos Baleba for the Premier League showdown with Aston Villa, while Harry Maguire and Patrick Dorgu are doubtful.

The Red Devils put a stop to their winless run on Tuesday with a dramatic comeback 3-2 victory over Roma in the Champions League as Matheus Cunha netted a late brace to turn the game on its head.

Carrick had been under serious scrutiny following United’s worst ever start to a Premier League campaign, with his side slipping into the relegation zone following Nottingham Forest’s win over Manchester City on Saturday evening.

Now, however, they will be looking to build some momentum after a much-needed win.

There could be a return for Dorgu from injury after he made a surprise appearance in training before the Roma game, having been sidelined for over a month with a hamstring issue picked up on international duty.

As such, it could hand Carrick a more natural option at left-back, with Diogo Dalot filling in in that position in recent games.

There will also be no place in the squad for Lisandro Martinez, who serves his one-match suspension after his red card in the defeat at Chelsea, while Maguire is expected to be fit despite limping off late on against Roma.

In the engine room, Baleba pulled up with a hamstring injury against Roma, and is now set for an extended spell on the sidelines.

“Carlos we don’t know exactly [the severity], but it’ll be a number of weeks yet,” Carrick said of the midfielder in Friday's pre-match press conference.

“Definitely not this week and not over the international break, it will be a little bit longer yet.”

Kobbie Mainoo is likely to retain his place and potentially alongside Youri Tielemans - against his former club - behind captain Bruno Fernandes in the No10 role.

It has been widely reported that Shea Lacey will replace Amad Diallo on the right with Bryan Mbeumo up top, in lieu of Benjamin Sesko, who is out until the new year with a shin problem.

#1751. Liverpool XI vs Crystal Palace: Starting lineup, confirmed team news, injury latest for Premier League today

Dominik Szoboszlai returns to Liverpool’s starting lineup against Crystal Palace today.

The Hungarian international replaces Trey Nyoni in midfield, with Ryan Gravenberch still sidelined.

The Dutchman, who was dropped for last weekend’s 1-0 home defeat by Arsenal, missed the Champions League loss against Fenerbahce due to a heel injury that prevented him from travelling to Istanbul.

Gravenberch’s availability for the weekend had remained up in the air, with head coach Andoni Iraola revealing the midfielder was in a race against the clock to prove his fitness ahead of the trip to Selhurst Park.

“The only doubt we will have is Ryan,” the Liverpool head coach said at Friday’s pre-match press conference. “The others will be the same as we have been.

“The Ryan Gravenberch thing is a day-to-day thing, it’s a matter of pain. Let’s see if he can deal with the pain and he can help us.”

With Gravenberch remaining unavailable due to injury, the temptation to use Szoboszlai deeper and play Florian Wirtz in the No10 role has proven too much for Iraola.

Alisson Becker is under some scrutiny over his performances after the defeat by Fenerbahce, following on from his mistake against Arsenal.

The Brazilian, who has not been called up by Carlo Ancelotti for international duty this month, starts against Palace, with Milos Kerkez and Ronald Araujo restored to the full-back positions after being named on the bench in Istanbul.

Alexander Isak’s impressive scoring streak may have ended against Arsenal, but the Swede bagged a seventh goal in 13 appearances with his maiden Champions League strike of the season against Fenerbahce.

Isak came off the bench to grab his goal, but he starts at Selhurst Park. Bradley Barcola is restored to a more familiar wing role after his experiment up top, with Dutchman Cody Gakpo reintroduced on the other flank.

#1750. Mourinho: Winning at Real Madrid is normal

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jose Mourinho joked Real Madrid have a "happy dressing room, with horrible music" as he reminded his players that winning is an expectation at the club.

Madrid beat 10-man Valencia 3-0 on Saturday to move level on points with LaLiga leaders Barcelona.

Federico Valverde, Arda Guler and Kylian Mbappe were on target for Los Blancos, who have won their last eight games in all competitions, since a loss to rivals Atletico Madrid on September 20.

And while Mourinho is delighted with Madrid's form and squad unity, he says his team are aware of the lofty expectations at Madrid.

"What makes me happy is that we've never had chaos; we've always been calm," Mourinho said.

"We understand the reasons why we lost [against Atlético] and where we could improve.

"I will always fight to ensure that in good times, people stay balanced. I always tell them that winning matches in a team like Real Madrid shouldn't lead to crazy joy. Winning matches at Real Madrid has to be normal.

"I see a happy dressing room, with horrible, loud music.

"When we lose, we enter your chaos, which can then spread to the Madridista environment, to the fans. But in here, we're calm."

— Real Madrid C.F. (@realmadriden) November 8, 2026

Mourinho is now on 97 wins in charge of Madrid in LaLiga, across his two spells in charge.

Only three other coaches in Madrid's history have hit a century of wins in the top flight.

Mourinho has overseen 126 LaLiga games, meaning his 77% win ratio is the best of any coach to have taken charge of 100+ games in the competition.

Madrid face Celta Vigo after the international break, and Mourinho conceded it is always worrying when his players head off for duty with their countries.

"It worries me, because if the players stayed with me and my staff we would give very special attention to recovering them," he said. "But they go to their national teams.

"I have never coached a national side, but you can imagine that their coaches want to work, and these people can't work now. They need to rest. They need a lot of attention in their recovery."

#1749. Chelsea XI vs Sunderland: Starting lineup, confirmed team news, injury latest for Premier League today

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Moises Caicedo is fit to start for Chelsea against Sunderland today, but Emi Martinez is not in the matchday squad.

The Blues midfielder had emerged as a slight doubt for the Premier League clash at the Stadium of Light as he was not spotted during the 15 minutes of Wednesday’s training session that was open to the media.

Xabi Alonso then revealed Caicedo’s absence was due to discomfort he felt after the Manchester United match, confirming the final training session before the trip to Sunderland, on Saturday, would be used as a guideline for the midfielder’s availability.

Caicedio’s social media activity suggested he would be fine to start in midfield and that is the case as he is joined in the engine room by Romeo Lavia and former Sunderland midfielder Jordan Henderson, who has recovered from illness.

The Blues head to the Stadium of Light hoping to build on last Saturday’s 2-0 win over 10-man United at Stamford Bridge.

Young goalkeeper Mike Penders kept a clean sheet in that game as summer signing Martinez continued his recovery from surgery following the fractured jaw he suffered in last month’s victory against Everton.

But Martinez - wearing a protective face mask - was this week involved in Chelsea training at Cobham to raise suggestions of an early return, but he is not included in the squad at all.

Previously injured Argentine defender Aaron Anselmino has also been involved in training, after being selected to play for his country over the upcoming international window.

Estevao started against United and impressed, but drops down to the bench.,

Joao Pedro and Maxence Lacroix are both still sidelined, along with Jorrel Hato and captain Reece James, who is recovering from knee surgery and unlikely to be available again until January.

Winger Jamie Gittens suffered an ankle injury on international duty with England’s Under-21s last month. He will be out for “a few weeks”, Alonso said a fortnight ago.

Chelsea XI vs Sunderland (3-4-2-1): Penders; Palestra, Fofana, Colwill, Chavarria; Lavia, Caicedo (c), Henderson; Palmer, Neto, Rogers

#1748. Man United transfer news: Liverpool, Red Devils among clubs chasing Serie A 'rising talent'

By Darren Plant | 07 Nov 2026 12:09

Liverpool and Manchester United have allegedly identified AC Milan defender Koni De Winter as a potential transfer target.

The two North-West rivals are currently preparing for their final Premier League fixtures before the November international break.

Andoni Iraola's side face Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park before Michael Carrick's outfit square off against Aston Villa at Old Trafford later on Sunday.

Despite the clubs sitting at opposite ends of the Premier League table, it has become apparent that they each need to strengthen in the defensive third of the pitch.

According to Caught Offside, De Winter has emerged as a possible addition for both clubs.

The report alleges that scouts have been 'closely monitoring' the 24-year-old in recent weeks.

De Winter has made a total of 13 starts and one substitute outing in Serie A and the Europa League this season.

Although AC Milan have been inconsistent under Ruben Amorim, the Belgium international is seemingly enhancing his reputation at San Siro.

Nevertheless, it is said that De Winter is currently not actively pursuing a move away from AC Milan.

He is currently only in his second campaign at the club since leaving Genoa, while the eight-cap international has been given a more trusted role under Amorim than by his predecessor in 2025-26.

While De Winter is seemingly progressing well under Amorim, that does not necessarily mean that he is the right choice for Liverpool or Man United.

In the latter's case, they could benefit from proven Premier League quality being added to their defence, as well as someone who can eventually replace Harry Maguire.

Similar applies with Liverpool. Even if Jeremy Jacquet, Ronald Araujo and Giovanni Leoni are viewed as three strong centre-back options for the future, the Merseyside giants will likely target someone more experienced than De Winter to replace Virgil van Dijk.

#1747. Report: Liverpool want to hijack transfer for midfield sensation

Ever since Arne Slot took over from Jurgen Klopp at the start of the 2024-25 season, Liverpool's midfield has been an issue.

Even though the German managed to figure out a system that worked, it still wasn't perfect.

Fabinho's exit is one of the main problems that the Reds have faced recently with the club failing to sign his replacement almost three years later.

Indeed, some youngsters such as Stefan Bajcetic, Tyler Morton and Ryan Gravenberch have all been used to try and plug the gap but, nothing compares to having a natural number six in that role.

Fans have known that some serious money needs to be spent on their midfield for some time now but, for one reason or another, other areas of Liverpool's squad have been focused on instead.

But now, that seems like it's all about to change.

Liverpool are ready to battle Chelsea for the transfer of Lamine Camara

Lamine Camara's situation was a bit of a funny one in the summer.

Throughout most of the transfer window, he was linked with an exit from AS Monaco.

And, by deadline day, a deal was agreed with Chelsea and it looked like the Senegal international was going to make the move.

However, at the last minute, the Ligue 1 outfit pulled out of the deal with some journalists, such as Ben Jacobs speculating that Liverpool were the reason why Filipe Luis' men pulled out of the transfer.

Obviously, this left a sour taste in Chelsea's mouths but now, according to an update from Footy Africa, both clubs are going to go to war in January for Camara's transfer.

"Former Premier League champions Liverpool have become the latest club to show strong interest in signing Camara in the winter and are ready to battle Chelsea for the signature of the young Senegalese midfielder," they wrote.

"Andoni Iraola’s men failed to add a marquee signing in midfield over the summer and will now be keen to strengthen as they look to boost their title challenge.

"Additionally, the uncertainty over the future of Argentine midfielder Alexis Mac Allister is also expected to push their interest, especially as the former Brighton star could depart next summer."

Lamine Camara would be perfect for Liverpool

Of all the midfielders that Liverpool have been linked with, Camara would easily be one of their best options.

Although he wouldn't be homegrown, with Wataru Endo, Federico Chiesa and Kostas Tsimikas all likely to leave by the end of the season, those non-homegrown spots among the Reds' ranks will soon open up.

Signing Camara would obviously cost the Reds a decent chunk of change as, since the summer transfer window slammed shut, he's only got better.

And, since Chelsea are still eager to sign him, there's obviously going to be a bit of a scrap to get a deal for him over the line.

He's a natural defensive midfielder, can run forever and wins the vast majority of the duels that he attempts.

All of these skills are why he'd be perfect for Liverpool, even if he is likely to cost them an arm and a leg.

#1746. GdS: €100m at risk for Milan between Champions and Europa League – the breakdown

The ups and downs that AC Milan have experienced so far this season could prove costly in the end, as highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning.

Ruben Amorim’s tenure at the club has certainly been a mixed bag so far. While the results in the league have been okay with 21 points after 10 games, they have been the opposite in the Europa League with a mere three points after four games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As Gazzetta dello Sport reports this morning (see featured image), the problem isn’t just that Milan are struggling on the pitch, but also that it could have a massive effect on the finances. Between a top-four finish and a Europa League failure, we are talking about €100m.

Starting with the present, Milan have collected a mere €14.6m from the Europa League so far, excluding ticket sales for the games against Benfica and Ferencvaros. In other words, it’s just the guaranteed revenue plus the prize money for a win (€450k).

Direct qualification to the knockout phase, which was definitely the goal at the start, has now become rather difficult. Not even winning all of the remaining four games would be a guarantee, as that would take Milan to 15 points, and 16 might be required.

The feeling is that Milan have to focus on reaching the knockout play-offs instead. If they were to fail even with that, as the pink newspaper continues, we would be talking about a loss of €8m for the round of 16, between prize money and ticket sales.

Looking at the bigger picture, given that the Rossoneri among the favourites to win the competition in the summer, doing so would generate total revenue of €40m. Furthermore, lifting the trophy would secure qualification to the Champions League.

After missing the last two editions, failing to qualify yet again would be a massive failure for the entire RedBird project. This is especially true as the 2027-28 season will mark the beginning of a new cycle for UEFA in terms of commercial and TV rights, with numbers expected to significantly increase.

According to the newspaper, the total pot of prize money for the participating clubs will increase from the current €2.46bn to €2.8bn. For the Rossoneri, this would mean going from a minimum revenue of around €40m to around €50m, even before stepping onto the pitch.

To this figure, one must add around €10-15m from the ticket sales, so failure to qualify for the competition next season would mean missing out on a minimum of €60m (!). It could quickly rise to €70-80m too, so we really are talking about a lot.

Qualifying for the Champions League would increase the overall revenue by more than 20% and fuel Milan’s project of growth, especially since other improvements are on the cards too. For example, from 2028-39, Adidas will start paying €50m per season to the club.

Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

United continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

Worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

Foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

Heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

United are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

Good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

#1743. Report - Disaster: Agents of Liverpool star now in talks to leave, Reds desperate to keep him

Liverpool could lose yet another star. His agents are now in talks with a UEFA Champions League side as a potential exit is on the cards.

Liverpool have lost a lot of truly great talent over the last few years. Not all of it has been choice, either, though some of it absolutely was. Mohamed Salah leaving this year, for instance, was down to the club as much as the player.

There have been plenty of sales, too. Curtis Jones departed for Inter in the summer while homegrown talent like Caoimhin Kelleher and Jarell Quansah were both sold to starting positions elsewhere.

But then there are the ones that aren't by choice. Trent Alexander-Arnold was offered a new contract but rejected it to join Real Madrid. One year later, Ibrahima Konaté did literally the exact same thing.

And it likely won't stop there. That doesn't mean players will leave next year to join Real Madrid (but don't rule that out) but there are stars who could get their heads turned.

Bayern Munich were surprisingly linked with a move for Rio Ngumoha in the summer. They were supposedly willing to put up quite a bit of cash to make it happen, though Liverpool never entertained the idea.

But Christian Falk reports that they haven’t actually stopped looking. He claims that Bayern remain in talks with representatives of Ngumoha, though not directly the player himself.

They’re eager to find the player who could take over from Luis Diaz on the left wing. Ngumoha is certainly a fit for that - even if a successor to the Colombian is the exact same role that Liverpool want him for.

Now, the reason these talks are important is that Ngumoha’s contract expires in 2028 and Liverpool are in their own talks to get a new one signed. If they fail, there will be immense pressure to sell next summer while they can still get a fee for him.

That then becomes even more complicated because Chelsea get 20 per cent of any sale. Essentially, there’s no good outcome here other than Ngumoha re-signing with Liverpool.

Bayern are going to do all they can to make sure that doesn’t happen, though. We’ll probably refrain from predicting how this one goes, given the exits over the last couple of years, but we know Liverpool are pushing hard.

#1742. Crystal Palace vs. Liverpool: Andoni Iraola makes referee admission ahead of Selhurst Park visit

By Darren Plant | 07 Nov 2026 12:24

Andoni Iraola has reiterated that his Liverpool squad tend to be "too honest" during games.

Iraola made headlines last week when he suggested that he would tell his squad to "dive" when having their shirt pulled in future.

That claim was made after Alexander Isak failed to go down, or even react, to being pulled back in the Arsenal penalty area during the first half of their Premier League fixture.

Liverpool subsequently went on to suffer a 1-0 defeat to the Gunners, who now sit three points clear at the top of the Premier League table.

Speaking ahead of Sunday's Premier League game at Crystal Palace, Iraola suggested that he did not like his players being praised for their 'honesty'.

As quoted by Sky Sports, the Spaniard revealed that his players received 'congratulations' from the officials.

He said: "I don’t want to talk too much about referees. I think we are quite an honest group. Sometimes too honest, and even the other day after the game, I think the referee congratulated us.

"But I don’t know if I liked it a lot or not. But he said our behaviour has been very good overall from the players, from the staff.

"I think it has to be genuine, no? You cannot fake things. When we complain it has to be genuine complaints because I think it’s a penalty, it’s a yellow card, it’s whatever.

"I feel we are willing, obviously, we are a team that wants to press, wants to be intense, but I think the balance, there is a big difference, yes."

As per Opta, only two teams in the Premier League have been awarded fewer fouls than Liverpool.

For a high-profile club that will generally have more possession than other teams in the majority of their fixtures, it is an eye-catching statistic.

#1740. Opinion: Liverpool make Ronald Araujo decision, major update proves it

Ronald Araujo has been one of Liverpool's best signings this season.

The defender came to Anfield on a season-long loan in their time of need.

Most people thought that he would just be a back-up option that could cover centre-back and right-back if needed.

However, his stellar performances since the start of the campaign have led to him making the right-back spot his own with others such as Jeremie Frimpong and Joe Gomez failing to displace him.

As mentioned, he's only on a season-long loan at the moment with Liverpool's option to buy worth somewhere around €55 million.

This price tag has created a bit of a stumbling block for the Reds with a decision on his future now potentially being made.

Liverpool may sign Nmamdi Collins instead of Ronald Araujo

Liverpool's defence has been a major topic of conversation over the last couple of years.

Whether it's been players such as Trent Alexander-Arnold leaving or fans questioning why they spent £55 million on Jeremy Jacquet, the Reds' defence has always been a huge topic.

And, with Virgil van Dijk, Alisson and Gomez's contracts all expiring in June 2027, it's going to remain at the centre of attention for some time.

Figuring out what's going to happen with their current crop of players is likely to be one of the main things holding up a deal for Araujo.

But, as per a fresh update from Fussball News, a totally different target than the Uruguayan seems to have just made his way onto Liverpool's shortlist.

"According to information from fussball-news.de, Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool are all seriously interested in the Frankfurt defender. All three Premier League clubs are monitoring his development and regularly scout the young German international," they wrote.

"A departure from Frankfurt in the near future doesn't seem likely. The club from Hesse is planning for the long term with Collins and only recently secured his services with a contract extension until the summer of 2030.

"Nevertheless, the defender could become an interesting prospect in the upcoming transfer windows. "Collins' versatility is a major draw for top English clubs. The right-footed player can be deployed both in central defense and on the right side of defense.

"In addition, he possesses exceptional speed, physical presence, and tackling skills. Collins can particularly exploit his athletic strengths against fast attacking players."

Nmamdi Collins would be a better option for Liverpool than Ronald Araujo

Right now, fans would hate to see Araujo not get given a permanent deal.

However, since he'll be 28 years old by next summer, he may not have all that long left at the top.

Obviously, if his performances keep to this same level throughout the entire campaign, Liverpool will have to heavily consider signing him permanently.

But, it certainly won't hurt for them to weigh up their options.

Collins is much less experienced than Araujo and hasn't tried his luck outside of the Bundesliga yet but, since he's so important for Eintracht Frankfurt despite only being 22 years old, he's clearly an exceptional talent.

The report from Fussball News also goes on to say that a fee worth around €35 million is all that would be required for Liverpool to sign him.

This price tag is a much lower risk to Liverpool and since he's still so young, he could very easily grow to become an even better player than he already is.

At the moment, nobody knows what the Reds are going to do but, if their back line isn't a major area of focus again in the upcoming transfer windows, it'll be a massive shock.

#1738. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.
