Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP

Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

Haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a new campaign.

It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

“It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”

#1632. Club Leon vs CD Guadalajara - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 07 Nov 2026 23:56

Club Leon host Club Deportivo Guadalajara, known as Chivas, in the Liga MX Apertura 2026 at Estadio Leon (Nou Camp) on Monday.

Leon sit ninth on 22 points in the Liga MX Apertura table after Friday's matches and need results to hold a top-eight place, while Chivas are already through to the quarter-finals on 29 points and are chasing the top seed with America and Cruz Azul level on the same total.

Leon have 22 points from 15 matches, built on six wins, four draws and five defeats, with a goal difference of only +2 from 22 scored and 20 conceded.

That leaves La Fiera ninth after Friday's round, level on points with eighth-placed Tijuana, who hold a better goal difference of +3, with Monterrey one point behind on 21 and Pumas and Queretaro on 20.

Javier Gandolfi's side have gone two matches without a win, drawing 1-1 with Toluca at home on October 24 and then losing 2-1 at Cruz Azul on November 1, where Andres Montano converted a 56th-minute penalty, Jose Paradela added a second in the 72nd minute and Jose Alvarado replied only with a stoppage-time penalty.

The 3-5 home defeat by America on October 17 is the clearest warning for this fixture, because it belongs to a run of nine goals conceded in the last five matches, in which Leon have scored every time, eight in total, and won only once, 2-0 at Tigres on October 20.

Leon won both league meetings with Chivas in 2025 at the Nou Camp, 2-1 on January 28 and 1-0 on July 19, and the fixture has not ended level at Estadio Leon since November 2016, but the most recent meeting was a 5-0 defeat at Estadio Akron on March 18.

Gandolfi said after the Cruz Azul defeat that Liguilla qualification depends only on his own team, and the arithmetic backs him up: a win would take Leon to 25 points, a draw to 23, and a defeat would leave them on 22 before the final-round trip to Santos Laguna.

Chivas have 29 points from 15 matches, with eight wins, five draws and two defeats, and their 14 goals conceded is the lowest total in the league, against 25 scored.

Gabriel Milito's side have won three in a row, 1-0 against Necaxa on October 20, 1-0 at Monterrey on October 24, where goalkeeper Raul Rangel saved a penalty, and 4-2 against Atlante on October 31, after a four-match winless run in which they collected three points from 12.

The Atlante win was led by 18-year-old Santiago Sandoval, who scored twice as a false nine after Milito left Angel Sepulveda and Ricardo Marin on the bench, with Efrain Alvarez adding a goal and Diogo Bagui scoring an own goal.

Sandoval made his Liga MX debut as a substitute against Leon on July 19, 2025, scored both goals against Tigres in the Clausura quarter-finals and now has five league goals this tournament, level with Roberto Alvarado and Marin.

Chivas are the only team in the league without an away defeat, with three wins and four draws from seven road matches for 13 of 21 points, and both of their defeats this tournament came at the Estadio Akron.

America, Chivas and Cruz Azul are level on 29 points, with America ahead on a goal difference of +15 against Chivas' +11 and Cruz Azul's +10, and Chivas close the regular season at home to Cruz Azul on November 22, so a win at Leon would take them to 32 points.

Leon have no new injury concerns, although Jose Ramirez and Santiago Londono have been left out of Gandolfi's plans, Luis Valadez (foot injury), and Angel Estrada (fractured tibia) are not available.

Juan Guevara is one yellow card from a suspension, which matters for a back line that has conceded 20 goals, and Sebastian Vegas is also reported to be on four bookings.

Gandolfi is expected to keep the side that started at Cruz Azul, with Panama international Ismael Diaz, Edgar Guerra and Alfonso Alvarado leading the attack.

For the visitors, Miguel Tapias remains in rehabilitation and Miguel Gomez has returned to treatment after a muscle relapse.

Luis Romo returned to the starting lineup against Atlante after a biceps femoris injury suffered on Mexico national-team duty, and Jose Castillo, Brian Gutierrez and Angel Sepulveda are back in contention.

Milito is expected to stay with the lineup that beat Atlante, although Marin, who has five league goals, and Sepulveda are the options if he restores a nominal striker in place of Sandoval's false-nine role.

Garcia; Moreno, Romana, Guevara, Mora; Echeverria, Rodriguez, Arcila; Guerra, A. Alvarado, Diaz

Rangel; Campillo, Romo, Aguirre; Ledezma, Govea, R. Gonzalez, B. Gonzalez; Alvarez, R. Alvarado, Sandoval

The gap in the numbers points towards Chivas, who average 1.67 goals per game against a Leon defence that concedes 1.33, while Leon must break down a Chivas back line that has conceded only 14 goals and kept six clean sheets.

Leon have scored in each of their last five league matches and won both previous league meetings at the Nou Camp in 2025, so a goal for the hosts is likely, but they have taken only five points from their last five games and conceded in 11 of their 15 matches, and we expect Chivas to score twice and leave Leon needing a result at Santos Laguna on the final day.

#1629. Woltemade involved in both goals but VAR denies Lucumí as Juventus draw 2-2 with Rennes

Nick Woltemade created Juventus's opener and scored their equaliser, but Jhon Lucumí's late winner against Rennes was ruled out for offside. The draw in Turin moves Spalletti's side to seven points in the Europa League league phase ahead of Sunday's trip to Lecce.

Juventus came within a VAR decision of beating Rennes at the Allianz Stadium on Thursday 22 October. Jhon Lucumí found the net in the 90th minute. Referee Morten Krogh studied the pitchside monitor and disallowed the goal for offside. Eight minutes of stoppage time followed, and the match finished 2-2.

Nick Woltemade was central to both Juventus goals. Spalletti’s side now sit on seven points after three league-phase matches. They had lost 0-3 to Lazio in their previous game.

Zeki Çelik put Juventus ahead in the fifth minute from Woltemade’s pass. Mousa Al-Tamari equalised in the 15th minute, set up by Bryan Reynolds. Federico Gatti was booked in the 19th minute for stopping the Rennes goalkeeper from taking a quick clearance.

Weston McKennie hit the post at around the half-hour mark with the score still level. Rennes then won a penalty when Douglas Luiz was penalised for handball. Boulaye Dia converted it in the 43rd minute, and the visitors led 1-2 at the break. Çelik, the scorer of the opener, went off injured after 45 minutes. Al-Tamari earned the match’s top rating from the data provider, 8.2.

The equaliser came from the spot. Reynolds blocked a Nico González header with his arm away from his body, and VAR upheld the award. Woltemade scored the penalty in the 67th minute. He finished with seven shots and two key passes.

Juventus generated expected goals of 2.25 against 1.72 for Rennes. They also had 54% of possession. Rennes took more shots, 16 to 14, and put more on target, five to four. Juventus were caught offside three times, while the visitors were never flagged. Abdelhamid Aït Boudlal was booked in the 82nd minute for time wasting.

Both sides were short of key players. Spalletti was without the injured Locatelli, Yildiz, Thuram, Grabara, Ekhator and Conceição. Zhegrova and Milik were unavailable because they are not on the UEFA squad list. Antonio Stefano Merola was in the 21-man squad after his first senior call-up. Rennes were missing their leading scorer Lepaul, who was injured and did not travel from France.

FT |⌛️| Finisce in parità all’Allianz Stadium#JuveSRFC #UEL pic.twitter.com/QaF2LuUDp9

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) October 22, 2026

Krogh had refereed nine Europa League matches and one Champions League match before this game. He had never taken charge of either club.

Juventus’s next Europa League fixtures are away to AZ Alkmaar on 5 November 2026 and at home to Omonia on 26 November 2026. Before that, Serie A resumes. Lecce host Juventus on matchday 8, with Eusebio Di Francesco’s side kicking off against Spalletti’s at 18:00 Italian time on Sunday 25 October.

Everton could look to make a major statement in the January transfer window as David Moyes considers ways to strengthen his side’s attacking options.

After concerns over the team’s lack of goals, the Toffees are reportedly exploring a move for a forward with proven Premier League experience.

Manchester United’s Marcus Rashford has emerged as a potential target, with reports suggesting Everton are discussing the possibility of bringing the England international to Merseyside.

A deal would give Moyes another versatile attacking option, although several key details would need to be resolved before a transfer could progress.

According to Football Insider, former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness believes a move for Rashford is being discussed seriously ahead of the January window.

Speaking on Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, Wyness said: “Yes, this is definitely being talked about and quite strongly. And I think that could be an interesting solution.”

The former Everton chief executive also pointed to Rashford’s previous loan spells and suggested that a move closer to Manchester could benefit the player.

“Rashford did well when he was on loan at Villa and at Barcelona as well. I think it could work, and I think being close to where he is in Manchester, just along the M63, could also benefit him greatly as well,” Wyness explained.

The comments suggest that a January switch is a possibility worth monitoring, although neither club has confirmed an agreement. Separate reporting from FootballTransfers has also indicated that Everton and Manchester United have held early discussions over a potential winter move.

Wyness drew comparisons with Jack Grealish, who has made an impact at Everton when available, adding: “We’ve seen Jack (Grealish) moving across that way as well, and when he’s fit, Jack is certainly a big asset for Everton. He then added: “I wouldn’t be surprised to see something happening in January.”

For Everton, Rashford’s versatility could be a major attraction. Although he has often operated from the left, he can also play centrally, potentially giving Moyes additional options across the frontline. His arrival could provide support for Thierno Barry and help address the team’s need for more goals.

However, the financial structure of any deal would be important. Everton would need to consider Rashford’s wages, Manchester United’s valuation and whether a permanent transfer or loan arrangement would be realistic. The forward’s willingness to join another Premier League club would also be a significant factor.

Rashford could represent an ambitious addition for Everton if the club can find an agreement that works financially. His Premier League experience and ability to operate in several attacking positions would give Moyes greater flexibility, while a change of environment could offer the player a fresh start.

The comparison with Grealish is particularly relevant to Everton’s approach. The club could look to provide Rashford with an environment in which he can rebuild his confidence and contribute more consistently, although any potential success would depend on his fitness, form and role within the team.

Nevertheless, a transfer is far from guaranteed. The reported discussions remain at an early stage, and Everton must still resolve the financial details and establish whether Rashford would be open to the move.

For now, Wyness’s comments add weight to speculation surrounding Everton’s January plans. If negotiations progress, Rashford could become a name to watch as Moyes looks to strengthen his attacking options for the second half of the season.

#1626. Celik and Nico Gonzalez injuries add to Juventus absences before Lecce

Juventus will travel to Lecce without Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez after both players picked up muscle injuries in Thursday’s 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes, adding two more names to an already long absence list for Luciano Spalletti.

The club confirmed the diagnoses in an official medical update on Friday, October 23. Both players had felt muscle discomfort after the Rennes match and went for tests at J|medical that morning.

According to the club, Celik has a low-grade injury to the biceps femoris in his left leg, while Nico Gonzalez has a low-grade injury to the soleus muscle in his right calf. Juventus said both players have already started their rehabilitation programmes, but the statement did not give a return date for either of them.

Medical Update | Çelik and Nico González’s conditions

🗞️ https://t.co/BHwNzeidQ7 pic.twitter.com/YUXRK97IwL

— JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 23, 2026

The timing is frustrating for Celik in particular. The Turkish full-back opened the scoring against Rennes in the fifth minute, converting a pass from Nick Woltemade, before being taken off at half-time. You can read how the rest of that night unfolded in our report on the Rennes draw.

Juventus have not put a timeframe on either recovery, so any estimate comes from the Italian press. Virgilio Sport reports that both players are expected to be out for around 20 days and should only return after the November international break, with the home game against Venezia on November 22 named as the first realistic target.

If that estimate holds, the pair would miss the trip to Lecce, the meeting with Genoa, the home game against Napoli, the Europa League visit to AZ Alkmaar and the match with Fiorentina. That is a demanding run to face with a thinner squad, and it comes at a point when Juventus are trying to recover from the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio.

Celik and Nico Gonzalez join Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Francisco Conceicao on the sidelines, according to Tuttosport. Conceicao is already in rehabilitation after the shoulder problem he picked up against Lazio, as covered in our Francisco Conceicao injury update.

Tuttosport’s expected line-up has Spalletti sticking with a 3-5-2, with Pierre Kalulu and Andrea Cambiaso on the flanks and Woltemade partnering Randal Kolo Muani in attack. The match at the Via del Mare kicks off at 18:00 Italian time on Sunday, October 25, with Maresca as referee.

Supporters will also have to wait until matchday to hear from the coach. Tuttosport reports that Spalletti, in agreement with the club, will not hold his usual press conference on the eve of the Lecce game. The paper links the decision to the packed schedule after the Europa League fixture, and Virgilio Sport notes that Spalletti has taken the same approach before during congested spells, with no controversy behind the choice.

The squeeze on the squad is now the bigger story. With two more first-team players ruled out and the injury list still growing, Spalletti will need his remaining options to carry the load through a busy stretch of Serie A and European fixtures before the international break.

#1625. Sunday's Premier League predictions including Man Utd vs. Aston Villa, Crystal Palace vs. Liverpool

By Matthew Cooper | 08 Nov 2026 00:00, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 00:00

Today's Premier League predictions include Manchester United at home to Aston Villa, before struggling Crystal Palace take on Liverpool.

High-flying Brighton & Hove Albion will welcome Brentford to the Amex Stadium for Sunday's Premier League encounter.

The Seagulls head into the weekend in third spot in the Premier League table, while the Bees start matchday 10 in sixth position.

Brighton have scored at least three goals in each of their five competitive home wins this season, and while Brentford have drawn all four of their away league games this term, we think the Seagulls will make full use of their firepower to extend their unbeaten head-to-head home run with a relatively comfortable victory.

Ipswich Town play host to Bournemouth on Sunday afternoon looking for the win that could catapult them into the top half of the Premier League table.

While the Tractor Boys start the next batch of fixtures in 14th position, the Cherries are in eighth place after three successive victories in the top flight.

Ipswich will feel that their lighter schedule and week off from action gives them a clear advantage for this contest. However, we cannot back against a Bournemouth side who are free-scoring and searching for their eighth successive victory in all competitions.

Liverpool will hope to bounce back and deliver a fatal blow to Pierre Sage's hopes of remaining in charge of Crystal Palace when the two clash in the Premier League on Sunday at Selhurst Park.

The Reds are sixth in the top flight with 15 points after nine matchweeks, and the come into the weekend on the back of a 3-2 defeat against Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday, whereas Palace are 18th with just seven points and could end the weekend in last place.

Palace may boast the advantage of playing at home, but their lack of options in attack could cost them.

While Liverpool have been far from perfect in the final third, they have often taken three points from Selhurst Park, and it would not be surprising if they claimed another victory on the road this weekend.

Needing nothing short of a minor miracle to replicate their 2025-26 feats against Chelsea, Sunderland host the Blues in Sunday's Premier League fixture at the Stadium of Light.

The Black Cats trail their visitors by 16 places and 11 points in the Premier League table at the time of writing and face Xabi Alonso's well-rested men after a sobering defeat in Europe too.

Fatigue should not play a significant role for Sunderland on Sunday given the alterations Le Bris made in midweek, but backing the Black Cats to get anything out of any Premier League game at present is a tough ask.

Therefore, even a Pedro-less Chelsea side - working on a full week's worth of rest - should stroll to victory, with an increasingly familiar clean sheet in tow.

Desperate to steer clear of the Premier League's relegation zone, Manchester United will host Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

The Red Devils are hoping to build on their midweek Champions League victory, while the Lions are keen to get back on track after a three-game winless run.

Man United may have won in midweek, but they were the beneficiaries of major errors from the Roma defence, and are unlikely to repeat the feat on Sunday.

Villa are on a three-game winless run that has spanned three different competitions, yet they will be optimistic about getting the better of their struggling hosts.

#1624. Chelsea considering “massive bid” for Spain international as PSG also circle

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Chelsea could make another major investment in their attacking options as they assess potential additions ahead of the January transfer window.

With the Blues continuing to build a squad capable of competing for major honours, Barcelona midfielder Fermín López has reportedly emerged as a player of interest.

The 23-year-old Spain international has attracted attention from several European clubs, with Paris Saint-Germain also considering a move.

Chelsea previously attempted to sign López in 2025, and fresh reports suggest the London club could revisit their interest if the opportunity arises.

According to CaughtOffside, Chelsea and PSG are both prepared to make significant offers for López, who remains an important part of Barcelona’s plans under Hansi Flick.

A source with links to the agents industry told CaughtOffside: “PSG are preparing a serious offer worth around €80million for Fermin Lopez,” before adding: “Chelsea are also considering a massive bid.”

The reported interest could set up a transfer battle between the Premier League side and the French champions. However, neither club has confirmed a formal bid, and any deal would depend on Barcelona’s position and the player’s willingness to leave his boyhood club.

Chelsea are familiar with López, having reportedly made a significant offer for him in the summer of 2025. The midfielder opted to remain at Barcelona, but the latest reports suggest the Blues could be willing to return if his circumstances change.

López’s ability to operate as an attacking midfielder, contribute goals and create chances makes him an appealing option. His performances have also strengthened his reputation as a versatile attacking talent capable of influencing games from advanced positions.

Competition for places at Barcelona could be one factor to monitor, although there is no confirmation that López is actively seeking an exit. CaughtOffside reports that Chelsea and PSG currently have the most concrete interest, while Arsenal and Manchester United have also made enquiries about his situation.

Barcelona, meanwhile, would reportedly prefer to retain the midfielder but could face pressure to consider substantial offers amid their financial challenges. López signed a contract extension in February 2026, keeping him at the club until 2031, meaning negotiations would likely require a significant financial commitment.

Chelsea may also have other priorities for January. The report identifies Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott as a potential focus for the Blues, meaning any pursuit of López could depend on how their wider transfer plans develop.

#1623. Serie A preview: Genoa vs. AC Milan – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

A tough away trip awaits AC Milan on Sunday afternoon, hoping to restore some order against an in-form Genoa side.

What many hoped would be a positive week quickly turned into a negative one, as Milan failed to build on the derby win against Ferencvaros. In other words, they need to respond with a strong performance against Genoa, which is easier said than done.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim didn’t have a press conference earlier today due to the tight schedule, so there are no new takeaways from him. Judging from the post-match interviews on Thursday, however, he’s expecting a lot more from his players at the Marassi.

Game date: Sunday, November 8 Kick-off time: 15:00 (CET) Venue: Stadio Luigi Ferraris Referee: Davide Massa (VAR: Camplone)

It’s been said for quite a few games now, but Amorim certainly isn’t being helped by the injury situation. In total, seven players will be on the sidelines for the game tomorrow, including key players like Samuel Chukwueze, Strahinja Pavlovic and Alexis Saelemaekers.

Milan were hoping to recover the Serbian for this one, but severe stomach pain is keeping him on the sidelines after missing the Ferencvaros game too. Considering that Matteo Gabbia and Fikayo Tomori were already on the injury list, it’s certainly not ideal.

Mike Maignan will be back between the sticks, at least, after serving a suspension in the Europa League. He will have a defence of Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara and Pervis Estupinan ahead of him, with the left flank being the main worry there.

In midfield, Ardon Jashari will be demoted to the bench as Luka Modric will be back from start, partnering with Yunus Musah in a tandem. Adrien Rabiot, meanwhile, is expected to have a slightly more advanced role.

Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic will be the danger men on the attacking flanks, looking to replicate their success against Inter in the derby. The same cannot be said for Goncalo Ramos, who instead needs to get going with his goalscoring after bagging just two league goals so far.

In terms of firepower on the bench, Amorim could turn to Davide Bartesaghi, the aforementioned Jashari, Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cisse. Francesco Camarda will also be there, of course, but whether he can be categorised as an impact player is a different question.

Predicted Milan XI (4-2-3-1): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Estupinan; Musah, Modric; Moreira, Rabiot, Pulisic; Ramos.

Predicted bench: Torriani, Bouyer, F. Terracciano, Vladimirov, Bartesaghi, Jashari, Comotto, Hutchinson, Cisse, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Chukwueze, Gabbia, Loftus-Cheek, Pavlovic, Saelemaekers, Terracciano, Tomori.

After what was a disastrous start to the 2025-26 season under Patrick Vieira, sitting rock bottom between the 7th and 9th matchdays, Daniele De Rossi was appointed. He quickly brought them above the relegation zone and managed to keep them there, finishing seven points clear in the end.

It was only right to confirm him for this season, as such, and there have been no regrets so far. The start was admittedly dodgy, with one draw and four defeats in the first five games, but there have been four wins and one defeat in the five games since. Crisis very much averted.

The only defeat in the last five games came against De Rossi’s former club as well, namely Roma, who have been on fire at the start of this season. There can be no accusations of the former midfielder throwing the game to benefit his former club, let’s put it that way.

Nevertheless, the poor star has been cancelled out and it’s possible that De Rossoneri just needed some time, especially after losing key players like Jeff Ekhator (to Juventus) and Brooke Norton-Vuffy (to Hull City). The Serie A veteran Ruslan Malinovskyi also waved goodbye as his contract expired.

On the flip side, the Rossoblu did keep hold of most of the key players from last season, such as Johan Vasquez, Leo Ostigard, Morten Frendrup, and Lorenzo Colombo. The latter was signed permanently from Milan after a season-long loan, as the conditions for the obligation were triggered.

Some interesting signings were also made, from the veteran (and former Milan man) Stephan El Shaarawy to the familiar face Hamed Traore, who played for Sassuolo between 2019 and 2013. After spells at Bournemouth, Napoli, Auxerre and Marseille, he’s now looking to regain stability.

As for the latest team news, De Rossi has a much better situation than Amorim with no injuries or suspensions to note. Lorenzo Venturino and Elias Havel were both on the sidelines but have returned for this one.

It looks like the former Milan men El Shaarawy and Colombo will start, while Junior Messias could perhaps be introduced from the bench. De Rossi didn’t give much away during his presser in terms of the team selection, but he did make it clear that Genoa cannot get too cocky.

Genoa (3-5-2): Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ellertsson, Baldanzi, Frendrup, Traore, El Shaarawy; Colombo, Osmajic.

Predicted bench: Stolz, Sommariva, Messias, Otoa, Sabelli, Puczka, Amorim, Meichtry, Mitaj, Vitinha, Sow, Drameh, Ehizibue, Wiafe, Venturino, Havel.

This will be the 157th encounter between the two sides, with Milan looking to build on their 71 wins in the fixture, while Genoa are quite far behind at 37 wins. 48 games have ended all square, which is a tally that has increased lately.

In the last five games, there have been three draws (3-3, 0-0 and 1-1), but the good news for the Rossoneri is that they won the other two games. The five games before that were all wins as well, with no defeat recorded against the Rossoblu since 2020.

The most recent win was a 2-1 win at the Marassi in favour of Milan, courtesy of goals from Christopher Nkunku and Zachary Athekame. They both left the club on loan this summer, so they won’t be of any help tomorrow.

In the game before that, Rafael Leao (another player who’s no longer in the team) rescued a point in the dying minutes after Colombo had given Genoa the lead in the first half.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in their last 10 Serie A matches against Genoa (W6 D4). Since 2020-21, the Rossoneri only have a longer run of unbeaten games against Hellas Verona (12).

➤ Milan have won each of their last four Serie A away games against Genoa; only against three teams do the Rossoneri currently have a longer running away win streak in the competition: Hellas Verona (seven), Messina (five) and Pisa (five).

➤ Genoa are on a three-game winning streak in Serie A. The last time the Rossoblu recorded a streak of four consecutive wins in a single season in the top flight was between March and April 2009.

➤ Genoa have won three of their first six home games this season (D1 L2). The Rossoblu haven’t won four of their first seven Serie A home games since the 2015-16 season, when Gian Piero Gasperini was in charge.

➤ Ruben Amorim’s Milan have scored 21 goals in their first 10 Serie A games this season. The last Rossoneri manager to do better after his first 11 league games was Cesare Maldini in 1972, with 25 goals.

➤ Milan have won two and drawn three of their first five away games this season. The Rossoneri have avoided defeat in their first six away games of the season on three occasions between 2020-21 and 2025-26, the same number as Inter and Napoli, and could now become the only team to do so four times in this span, including the current season.

➤ Genoa have scored four goals in the first 15 minutes of Serie A action this season, a figure they share with Frosinone, Atalanta, Lazio, and Roma and second only to Milan (five). However, the Rossoblu are the only team yet to score in the final 15 minutes of a match.

➤ Stephan El Shaarawy, who scored 21 goals in 83 league appearances for AC Milan, has provided an assist in each of his last two Serie A appearances. Should he also contribute to a goal in his next match, he would become, at 34 years and 12 days, the second-oldest player to achieve this feat in three consecutive games for Genoa since 2004-05, after Domenico Criscito in 2021 (34 years and 269 days).

➤ Adrien Rabiot has bagged five goals and three assists in his first eight league appearances this season. The last midfielder to do better in the first nine games of a Serie A season was Sergej Milinkovic-Savic in 2022-23, with 10 contributions (three goals and seven assists).

Furthermore, the Frenchman has been involved in a goal in each of his last five appearances, and the last Milan midfielder to do better in Serie A was Kaka in 2004 (seven).

➤ Diego Moreira has been directly involved in seven goals (four goals and three assists) in his first six Serie A appearances for AC Milan. Since 2004/05, no player has had more in his first six league games for the Rossoneri, equaling Mario Balotelli’s record (seven in 2013).

Starting with Milan, and at the back, I think we should keep an extra eye on Diawara. He did well in the derby but after switching to centre-back for the Ferencvaros game, his display just wasn’t good enough. He will have the same position tomorrow and we need to see an improvement.

Further up the pitch, Moreira showed in the derby that he can be just the X-factor that Milan need, and this game should be an even better one for him (at least on paper). The cameo against Ferencvaros was positive despite the result, so hopefully he can build on the last week.

As for the home side, I’m curious to see Traore in action again. He definitely had some very good games for Sassuolo against the Rossoneri and with more consistent playing time at Genoa, he could rediscover that spark which made him so special.

Finally, I think it would be silly to ignore the defensive general, Vasquez. He always seems to have good games against Milan and honestly, he’s the type of player the Rossoneri could use right now, at least as a deputy.

It’s been incredibly hard to predict how well Milan will do so far this season, with many ups and downs. However, my gut feeling tells me that they will be able to do a whole lot better than on Thursday, especially since the key players are back from start.

My only worry is the left-hand side of the defence, with Diawara and Estupinan set to start there. As such, I’m going to go for a narrow win, with no clean sheet either. Let us know your prediction in the comments below!

It seems like Milan is biggest own enemy in last couple of seasons. To predict this match is basically to predict how they are going to enter into the game.

Team must go for the win because this season and today position is opening opportunity to reach top positions.

Milan will win this game but again depend on the rotation. Personally I think why Milan can’t play consistently because of the heavily rotation. You cant gel into the games if too many changes each every game. They should just change 1 or two every game. Even when you want to rest certain key players. Just substitute them by half time instead.

#1622. Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

“It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca said, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”

His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

Marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he said. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”

His team showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

They could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his new manager.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

City will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a big ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “new Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a new season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2

The Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

Emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

Maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

Guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the new Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

Bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

City attempt to break down the left but Grealish just runs out of road.

Manchester City 1 Bournemouth 1 (Guehi) He might have missed a sitter earlier on, but when presented with a similar opportunity from a corner - this time via Cherki from the right - Guehi makes no mistake, planting his header beyond Petrovic.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

Haaland threatens to break free down Bournemouth’s right but Truffert just about recovers and clears his lines.

Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

Jebbison calls Donnarumma - who has been a spectator for the past 20 minutes - into action with a sharp header. There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

Foden goes into the book for a foul on substitute Jebbison. A tad harsh, perhaps. Looks like he semi-slipped into that contact.

Ayari attempts an bicycle kick but cannot beat Bizot. That would have been a goal of the month contender had it found the back of the net.

Guehi combines with Foden down the right and hits the by-line before a digging out a cross to Haaland. The ball is behind him and his right-footed effort does not have the requisite power to beat Petrovic, who has been immense today.

Bit better from City, Foden curls just wide, Semenyo has a shot well saved by Petrovic. Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. Obviously there will be further incomings but they are leggier and more haphazard than Bournemouth.

Chance! Foden, Nunes and Cherki work the ball from right to left on the edge of Bournemouth’s box, eventually falling to Haaland who scoops the ball over with his usually lethal left boot. The visitors had plenty of men between ball and goal and that caused the Norwegian to snatch at his effort.

Villa started last season with no win in their first five games and just three points. They then rallied strongly after that. This one feels different as the rebuild is so significant. Second half has been very flat so far.

City are asking questions now. Cherki combines with Foden down the right and the Englishman shifts the ball on to his favoured left boot and his curled effort deflects off Silva and out for a corner which comes to nothing.

Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

Kostoulas thinks he’s made it five having followed in a fizzed-in Costinha effort that had struck the post. But the strike is scrubbed off immediately and replays back up the linesman’s decision.

Little sign of City finding the composure to take control of this match. Passing is getting ever-sloppier and Guehi put a free header painfully wide. Maresca’s team are dominating possession but would be no surprise if the next goal was another Bournemouth sucker-punch. Kovacic and Cherki about to come on, the latter should improve the picture.

Anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

Dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

Nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

Shows how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

Brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

You’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

De Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

Villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

Play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

Boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

Pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four big summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

There’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

There’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

City now looking shaky at the back. Cross-field balls in their half zipping past half a dozen in sky blue without intervention, shots from range going just wide, Donnarumma needing to save well to prevent a second.

Has stopped clicking up front as well, something isn’t going to plan when you have Haaland in your team but most of the high balls are heading towards Foden and O’Reilly.

CARTÃO VERMELHO! Gomes is sent off. Disaster for Villa. It was a kick at Rutter borne of frustration. McGinn was already walking Gomes away from referee Peter Bankes before the decision came. A clear kick to the chest after Rutter knocked him over. Gomes has been nowhere near the level required. He will never forget his Villa debut.

Ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

Kluivert gets a sight at goal moments later but is denied by Donnarumma who gets down to his left sharply to keep the ball out.

Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

Moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

Villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

Some very untidy defending for the opening goal here which comes against the run of play, if not drastically so. Khusanov was bamboozled by an  innocuous high ball, couldn’t make decisive contact and left space for it to reach Evanlison on the right, whose cross was hard for Tavernier to miss.

A few groans and grumbles already from the home fans, Guehi getting some flak for squandering a decent position near the Bournemouth area and giving away the ball. Not really his job to be on the ball and making stuff happen near the opposition box though, is it?

This is looking very bad for Villa. Two Brighton goals in one minute for Jack Hinshelwood and it is 4-0 with 31 mins played. The first was a very well-worked goal – Ayari cross nodded down by Gomez for Hinshelwood to head in. The second was just another mistake by Villa – Ayari stealing the ball from Joao Gomes to create a critical turnover. Villa started well but they look completely outgunned physically. Brighton are really pressing home their advantage in the duels. Lots of pressure on the likes of young George Hemmings and Gomes.

"Absolutely INCREDIBLE!"Jack Hinshelwood scores two in a matter of minutes and Brighton are ripping Aston Villa apart! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tvS5qMJJ8C

Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) That’s two in a matter of seconds. Again, Villa try to play out from the back and again they get caught out. Ayari telescopes in a leg to take the ball away from Gomes on the edge of Villa’s box and Hinshelwood is there to tuck it home.

Brighton 3 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) A cross from the left is nodded back across goal by Gomez and Hinshelwood is there to finish.

Manchester City 0 Bournemouth 1 (Tavernier) Bournemouth carve City open with ease. A long ball from Smith is not dealt with and Rayan works the ball out to Evanilson who needs just a brief look up before picking out Tavernier, who finishes at the back post.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

City have not yet reached the intensity levels they usually show when in full swing. Semenyo tries to inject some energy with a burst down the left but Rayan does well to track back and cut it out.

Villa’s defence is floundering. This time a corner delivered from the right sails over everyone, including Bizot, but the back-post nod-down evades everyone and Villa clear their lines.

Bright start from City, but momentum has diminished since an odd miss from Haaland, whose limbs looked unusually muddled after O’Reilly soared down the left wing and crossed presentably. Move had an air of inevitability to it, was unexpected not to see the Norwegian score. Prepare the Samson similes.

The second goal from Brighton, and it’s direct. Georginio Rutter played through with a very straight ball, and Rutter had Pau Torres on the proverbial toast. De Cuyper kept up with his team-mate and ran onto the cross. Villa have not been bad. Torres, however, is having a dreadful afternoon.

Brighton 2 Aston Villa 0 (De Cuyper) Rutter does brilliantly to latch on to a ball over the top from well inside his half. He bursts down the left channel before lashing a fierce ball across the face of goal which De Cuyper turns in. Villa in all sorts of problems here.

What a start for Brighton!Maxim De Cuyper doubles their advantage! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/3WbyZlEhMV

Chance! O’Reilly bursts past Smith out on the left and picks out Haaland, who appears to be in two minds as to whether he wants to head or volley the ball. Instead he does neither and the chance goes begging.

Gomes leaves one on Ayari, which is risky given he has already picked up a booking. A red card at this point would be hugely damaging.

Brighton take the lead with an own goal from Victor Lindelof. An unfortunate one for the Swede who was trying to get Maxim De Cuyper’s shot off the line. It hit the post and ricocheted in off Lindelof. The fault lay with Pau Torres who gave the ball away needlessly. Very good turn from De Cuyper to make the room for the shot. Up until then, Villa - even with this unusual understrength side - were much the better.

Lewis is in fact playing right-back, with Guehi into defensive midfield alongside Anderson. O’Reilly advanced of both, with Gvardiol at left-back. All quite fluid, though, as you would expect from modern City.

Brighton 1 Aston Villa 0 (OG Lindelof) A disaster at the back for Villa. Pau Torres looks to play out from near the by-line but instead picks out De Cuyper inside Villa’s box. The wide man does well to steady himself before getting a shot away, which ricochets off the post, back on to Lindelof and into the net.

City have started brightly. Here Haaland slips in Lewis, who is unmissable with his new bleached hair, but Petrovic pulls off a smart save.

Chance! Ayari gets his pocket picked inside his own half by a buzzing Barkley. Buendia has a sight of goal but he slides the ball inches wide.

He’s at it again moments later, but he sends a third effort at goal over the bar.

Villa have started the brighter of the two sides. McGinn spins a deep free-kick into the box, which is cleared out to Buendia on the edge of the box but his shot sails over.

A warm minute’s applause for the former Manchester City manager.

Brighton are in their customary blue and white home kits shooting left to right, with Villa in black.

That’s a “Welcome Back Enzo” banner slowly cascading down the East stand. Feel that the tifo department has missed a trick, because it would have been very amusing to use a picture of Pep Guardiola, and see if anyone noticed. That could actually be Guardiola for all I know, my facial recognition is dreadful. Getting all of the trite “don’t they look similar!” observations out of my system ahead of the September cut-off point.

The teams have emerged from the tunnel at the Amex and the Etihad...

When asked by Sky Sports whether Ollie Watkins’ omission from the match-day squad was a sign that his Villa career was over, Emery pursed his lips and stared back at the reporter for a few seconds before saying: “Silence.”

After being pressed on the subject, he added: “No, no, no. We are playing today here. It’s OK. We are not speaking about [Ollie].”

"Silence" 🤫An unusual response from Unai Emery 😅 pic.twitter.com/kWNZtQu3PA

On taking charge of his first match as City head coach, Enzo Maresca told Sky Sports: “It’s big emotion. It’s a very nice feeling, the first game at home in front of our fans, so hopefully we can give them the three points.”

When asked about Elliot Anderson and the void left by Rodri, he added: “I think Elliot [Anderson] has to be himself; a good player, he’s going to be even better, but he has to be himself. Again, for me, there are no players that they are the same player, they are all different.

“We are happy with Elliot, but for sure, as we know, Rodri is a big player but he’s already gone. So now the focus is on the ones that are here with us and the ones that will probably arrive.”

Brighton and Hove Albion Verbruggen; Wieffer, Vuskovic, Boscagli, Dunk; Gross, Ayari; Gomez, Hinshelwood, De Cuyper; Rutter

Subs Steele, Strujik, Costinha, Svoboda, Osman, Yalcouye, David, Kostoulas, Yohanna

Subs Suzuki, Mings, Ruggeri, Bogarde, Alysson, Rowe, Burrowes, Garnacho, Lynch

Manchester City Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Lewis; Semenyo, Foden, O’Reilly; Haaland

Subs Rulli, Ait-Nouri, Nunes, Reis, Kovacic, Cherki, Gonzalez, Grealish, Marmoush

Bournemouth Petrovic; Smith, Silva, Hill, Truffert; Cook, Scott; Rayan, Kluivert, Tavernier; Evanilson

Subs Dennis, Diakite, Gannon-Doak, Toth, Sanchez, Brooks, Adams, Rodriguez, Jebbison

Brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he said of Guardiola’s grand design.

Tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s big idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

The Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for new signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

Representing Aston Villa 👊 pic.twitter.com/JjqgYhBzwb

TEAM NEWS! 🚨 Here's how we start 🆚 Villa! 👊 pic.twitter.com/nnFj5swsdg

Some eyebrows raised at the inclusion of Rico Lewis in City’s starting XI, presumably as a defensive midfielder given the presence of Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly and Khusanov on the team-sheet. He did not have a pleasant afternoon in Cardiff last weekend, although that could be said for several City players. Some lingering doubts about his physicality, in a Premier League becoming ever more hands-on, but Enzo Maresca knows him from his time as an assistant here and clearly rates him. Wonder whether that sentiment will endure if (when) City buy some new midfielders in the coming weeks.

🔵 TEAM NEWS🍒The first #afcb team of the new Premier League season 👊 pic.twitter.com/uJhTI01Jld

Haaland will make his 200th appearance for City this afternoon. Either Lewis or O’Reilly could be deployed alongside Anderson in central midfield.

Our first XI of the season! 🩵XI | Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Guéhi, Gvardiol, Lewis, Anderson, O'Reilly, Semenyo, Foden, HaalandSUBS | Rulli, Marmoush, Kovačić, Cherki, Nico, Grealish, Aït-Nouri, Reis, Nunes🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/6wSBoP8jon

Welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a new era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut…

The Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

Brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

#1621. Everton targeting Iceland international as Thierno Barry alternative

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Everton could make signing a new centre-forward a priority in January after entering the season short of options in attack.

David Moyes needs additional firepower to strengthen his squad, and a promising Iceland international has reportedly emerged as a potential solution.

Real Sociedad striker Orri Oskarsson is attracting interest from several Premier League clubs, with Everton understood to be paying particularly close attention to his progress.

The 22-year-old has impressed in Spain, and the Toffees could explore a move as they look to address a key weakness in their squad.

According to TEAMtalk, Everton are among the clubs monitoring Oskarsson ahead of the January transfer window. Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United, Sunderland and Brentford are also reportedly tracking the Icelandic forward, meaning Moyes could face competition if Everton decide to pursue a deal.

Everton’s need for a striker has become increasingly apparent following their summer business. Beto departed for Fiorentina without a replacement arriving, leaving Thierno Barry as the club’s only recognised centre-forward. Attempts to sign Folarin Balogun from Monaco and Joshua Zirkzee from Manchester United also failed to produce a deal.

That situation has reportedly encouraged Everton to examine their options ahead of January, with Oskarsson among the forwards attracting attention.

The Iceland international joined Real Sociedad from FC Copenhagen in 2024 and made progress during his previous campaign, scoring nine goals in LaLiga. His combination of physical presence, technical ability and finishing has helped establish him as an appealing prospect for clubs looking to strengthen their attacking ranks.

Oskarsson has also continued to impress at international level, with his performances for Iceland adding to his growing reputation. At 22, he could offer Everton both an immediate option up front and a potential long-term investment.

However, Everton would need to establish whether Real Sociedad are prepared to negotiate during the January window. The Spanish club invested significantly to secure his services, and there is no confirmation that they would be willing to let him leave midway through the season.

Oskarsson could be an important addition for Everton as Moyes looks to address the lack of depth at centre-forward. Relying heavily on Barry leaves the manager with limited specialist alternatives, particularly across a demanding second half of the campaign.

The Icelandic striker’s profile could suit Everton’s need for another option capable of leading the line. His technical qualities may also give Moyes greater flexibility in how the team approaches matches, while his age offers scope for further development.

Competition from Tottenham, Newcastle, Sunderland and Brentford could complicate Everton’s pursuit, however. The Toffees would need to move decisively if their interest develops into a formal approach, while the final cost and Sociedad’s willingness to sell would be key factors.

For now, Everton’s reported interest suggests the club are assessing potential solutions ahead of January rather than confirming a deal is imminent. With Moyes needing greater depth in attack, Oskarsson is a name to watch as the winter transfer window approaches.

#1620. Lecce vs Juventus: in-form hosts await Spalletti’s stretched side at the Via del Mare

Juventus face Lecce at the Stadio Via del Mare this evening, and the fixture arrives at an awkward moment for Luciano Spalletti. His side are still looking for a first win since the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio, while Di Francesco’s Lecce come into Matchday 8 on the back of their most convincing result of the season.

Kick-off is at 18:00 Italian time, which is 17:00 in the UK and Ireland.

Lecce travelled to Udinese last weekend and came away with a 3-0 victory. According to Flashscore, Kialonda Gaspar headed in the opener from a Gallo corner in the 14th minute, and N’Dri doubled the lead in the 25th minute after Tiago Gabriel had gone up for a header. Siebert added the third four minutes from time after a ball was won from Ekkelenkamp.

It was Lecce’s first win in Udine for six years and handed Udinese a fifth straight league defeat. Fatah also hit the crossbar, so the margin could have been even wider. For a side that has spent much of its recent history fighting at the wrong end of the table, it was a timely lift before the visit of Juventus.

The picture is very different in Turin. The heavy home loss to Lazio was followed by a 2-2 draw with Rennes in the Europa League, and the injury list has kept growing. Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez are the latest names to drop out, as covered in our Celik and Nico Gonzalez injury update, and Spalletti chose not to give a pre-match press conference on Saturday.

The Lazio defeat in Turin left Juventus well short of the Serie A leaders, so Sunday is about more than one result. Three points in Puglia would ease some of the pressure that has built up over the past week.

Juventus do not have to look far back for a good memory of this trip. The club’s own retrospective recalls the Matchday 36 meeting at the Via del Mare in May 2026, when Dusan Vlahovic scored after just 12 seconds. Kenan Yildiz started the move, Teun Koopmeiners was involved in the build-up and Andrea Cambiaso delivered the ball for Vlahovic to finish into the roof of the net.

That game stayed lively. Michele Di Gregorio had to make a fine save at the other end, Francisco Conceicao struck the crossbar and Vlahovic had another good chance, all inside the first six minutes. Pierre Kalulu thought he had added a second with around half an hour to play, but VAR ruled it out for a marginal Vlahovic offside in the build-up. The early goal proved enough for the win.

Several of the players involved that day, including Yildiz and Conceicao, are now injured, which shows how much Spalletti’s options have changed since May.

Tuttosport reports that Maresca will referee the match. In Italy it is live on DAZN and Sky. In the United Kingdom the game is shown on DAZN UK and Prime Video UK, in Ireland on DAZN, and in the United States on Paramount+, fuboTV and Peacock, according to the club’s broadcast guide.

Sources: Juventus FC, Juventus FC broadcast guide, Flashscore

At Juve FC, Luca covers match analysis, squad news, and the longer threads that run through a Juventus season. He writes with the perspective of someone who genuinely cares about where the club is heading rather than simply reporting what has already happened. His focus tends to lean toward how the team sets up, where things break down, and what needs to change to get back to where Juventus belongs in the European conversation.

#1619. Chelsea targeting Trent Alexander-Arnold as surprise transfer opportunity emerges

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Chelsea could be preparing for a significant change at right-back as the club assess their options ahead of the upcoming transfer windows.

With uncertainty surrounding Malo Gusto’s future at Stamford Bridge, the Blues have reportedly identified an unexpected target who could bring considerable experience and creativity to their defence.

Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold has emerged as a potential option, with former Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown suggesting the England international could be tempted by a move to west London if Chelsea decide to make an approach.

According to Football Insider, Chelsea are keeping tabs on Alexander-Arnold as questions continue over his role at Real Madrid. The 28-year-old has struggled to establish himself as a regular starter under Jose Mourinho, with competition for places limiting his opportunities.

Brown revealed that Chelsea are among the clubs monitoring the situation, telling Football Insider: “One name who I have heard in connection with a move to Chelsea is Trent Alexander-Arnold.”

He admitted the potential transfer had initially surprised him, adding: “It came as a bit of a surprise to me, to be honest, but he has fallen well down the pecking order at Real Madrid to the point where he’s now the second or even third choice.”

The former scout also questioned whether the defender currently fits into Mourinho’s plans, explaining:

“It appears Mourinho doesn’t rate him particularly in that right-back position, and he’s not the only one, because he’s been out in the cold for England as well.”

Despite those concerns, Brown believes Alexander-Arnold remains an attractive player because of his technical ability and reputation. Chelsea, meanwhile, have reportedly been assessing potential replacements for Gusto as they consider changes to their defensive options.

Brown added: “Alexander-Arnold is a talented footballer who has a very good skillset, but it is those weaknesses in his game that often raises concerns.”

He also suggested that Chelsea’s interest in high-profile players could make the move possible: “Chelsea, though, will always be keen on the possibility of signing a big-name player; it’s just what they do, so they’ll be keeping an eye on whether he does become available.”

The possibility of a return to Liverpool has also been discussed, but Brown believes Stamford Bridge could become a realistic destination if the defender decides to leave Spain.

“They’ll want to avoid that situation coming up again, as will he I expect, so Chelsea could be where he ends up and he could be tempted if they decide to make a move.”

However, Alexander-Arnold is not currently pushing for an exit. Previous reporting has suggested he wants to fight for his place at Real Madrid, meaning any potential Chelsea move would depend on how his situation develops.

#1618. Sunday's Serie A predictions including Napoli vs. Lazio, Inter Milan vs. Como

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 08 Nov 2026 00:00, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 00:00

Today's Serie A predictions cover an intriguing round of fixtures, with AC Milan travelling to Genoa, Juventus visiting Fiorentina and Atalanta BC taking on Monza, while Napoli host Lazio and defending champions Inter Milan welcome Como to the San Siro.

Trending in very different directions, Serie A leaders Lazio will visit a faltering Napoli side on Sunday, as Stadio Maradona hosts the lunchtime kickoff.

While the home side are struggling both in Europe and Italy's top flight, their southern rivals have posted nine wins from 10 and are yet to taste defeat in the league.

Struggling in Serie A, facing another early exit from Europe and burdened by a huge absence list, Napoli are set to lose three games on the spin.

While Lazio's stellar run will surely end soon, they can exploit their hosts' shaky defence and post a seventh straight win.

Atalanta BC will be looking to end a six-match winless run across all competitions when they travel to Monza on Sunday for matchday 11 of the Serie A campaign.

Maurizio Sarri's side sit 13th in the Italian top-flight table after collecting just 11 points from their opening 10 matches, leaving them four points above the relegation zone, where the hosts occupy 18th place.

Monza's defensive problems make it difficult to see them containing Atalanta, who have dominated this fixture in recent years, and that could provide the visitors with a good opportunity to end their current winless run.

After a week of highs and lows, AC Milan will head towards the international break with a tough trip to Genoa on Sunday afternoon.

Before they clash at Stadio Ferraris, the hosts have actually claimed more points from their last five Serie A games than the inconsistent Rossoneri.

Allied to two cup wins at Stadio Ferraris, Genoa have won half of their first six home games in Serie A, so Milan will be put through a stern test.

While Amorim's men are leaking too many goals, De Rossi's side have found their shooting boots, and that could produce an end-to-end draw.

Having suffered derby defeat and slipped off top spot in Serie A, reigning champions Inter Milan must try to get back on track when they welcome record-breaking Como to San Siro on Sunday.

Following four intense meetings last term, the regional rivals are currently separated by two points, with both trailing surprise leaders Lazio.

Inter's defence is creaking at the seams, and without the leadership of their inspirational skipper they are always more vulnerable.

Although free-flowing Como must be starting to tire, recent events suggest it is time to finally slay the Nerazzurri.

Sending Serie A into the international break, old foes Fiorentina and Juventus will clash at Stadio Franchi on Sunday night.

While the Viola are still seeking their first home win of the season, fallen giants Juve have been left trailing Italy's top six.

Both teams have been too inconsistent to match their pre-season aims, making the outcome on Sunday night quite tough to predict.

Juve are assured of a hostile reception in Florence, but the hosts tend to wilt in front of their own fans - so, all three points will go back to Turin.
