Possession: Fulham 61%-39% ChelseaShots: 14-18Shots on target: 6-6Corners: 6-4Touches in opposition box: 24-38

The final whistle is blown at Craven Cottage and Chelsea hold on to win 3-2 to give Xabi Alonso a win in his first game in charge. Alvaro Arbeloa’s first game as Fulham boss ends in defeat. An absorbing west London derby.

Garcia throws himself to the ground as Sessegnon sends in a cross but that is never going to be a penalty.

Will there be one more chance for Fulham to try and find an equaliser? Time is running out for the hosts.

Pedro has the ball in the back of the Fulham net but Quenda was offside in the build-up. A quick VAR check proves so.

Surely there is another goal in this one? It is a surprise there has not been since Garcia got a goal back for Fulham.

The latest booking of the game goes the way of Castagne, who cynically trips Colwill.

Sessegnon is played in down the left channel and flicks it past Acheampong inside the Chelsea penalty area. Sessegnon gets his shot away from a narrow angle and it is straight at Sanchez.

Palmer looks like he might have cramp in his calf and is going to be replaced by Estevao. Quenda also comes on for Chelsea, coming on for Rogers.

Fulham make an attacking alteration as Muniz replaces Robinson

That is a huge, huge chance for Fulham to equalise. Robinson is played in behind the Chelsea defence with a long ball in behind and Sanchez is in no-man’s land out of his goal. Robinson just has to lift it over Sanchez from the edge of the box but his effort goes wide. Fulham should be on level terms.

Fulham fans think they are about to be awarded a free-kick right outside the box but instead the free-kick goes the other way. It was a clear dive from Bassey, who is rightly booked for simulation.

James is the third Chelsea player into the book for cynically pulling King back. James then has the cheek to wag his finger at King, as if it was not a foul, yet it was a clear booking. James had to be careful there as some referees may not have taken too kindly to that.

Double change for Fulham as Kevin and Sessegnon are brought on.

That would have been a great goal from King. He has already scored once and is inches away from his second. He receives a pass on the turn from Robinson and drives towards the Chelsea box. He then cuts inside onto his right, beating Lacroix with ease, and nearly beats Sanchez at his near post but his shot goes inches wide.

This is a very open, end-to-end game and you would fully expect more goals in this one. I would be very surprised if this one ended 3-2. Both defences are looking leaky.

Fulham are going to make their substitution of the night as Charles comes on for his debut having signed from Southampton, replacing Bobb.

Enzo is being booed a lot by the home fans every time he touches the ball.

Chelsea are the first to turn to their bench. Enzo is coming on and is met by a lot of boos, mostly though from the home fans as the majority of the travelling Chelsea fans are applauding him. Chavarria is also on to make his Chelsea debut. Hato and Lavia head off.

There is a new rule being implemented. Hato takes far too long over a throw-in and Fulham are therefore awarded the throw-in instead.

When Palmer put Chelsea 3-1 up, the visitors looked in control of this match. Fast forward five minutes and the momentum has completely switched around. What an absorbing opening Monday night of the season!

The Fulham debutant gives them life and this game is not over. Castagne is found making a run in behind and cuts back inside onto his left inside the Chelsea penalty area. His shot is straight at Sanchez, who can only parry it straight into the path of Garcia, who heads into the ground and the ball bounces over Sanchez into the Chelsea net. Another poor piece of goalkeeping from Sanchez.

Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN

All members of Chelsea’s starting front three have got on the scoresheet tonight and Palmer also has an assist to his name.

Chelsea come close to a fourth as Hato squares it for Rogers inside the Fulham box but Robinson nips in just in front to clear.

He came close to scoring moments ago and now he does get on the scoresheet. Pedro gets onto the end of a flicked-on header by Rogers near halfway and drives into the Fulham half. As he gets to the Fulham penalty area, he waits for the overlapping run of Palmer and times the pass just right. Palmer, from a narrow angle, puts it between Leno’s legs and into the far corner.

"Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq

Palmer does brilliantly down Chelsea’s right to skip past a number of defenders and moves into the Fulham penalty area. He opens up his body and curls one towards the far corner. He is adamant that there is a deflection but a goal kick is given. Replays show Palmer may have had a point.

Nottingham Forest are ramping up their pursuit of Chelsea’s Liam Delap as Oliver Glasner eyes two major signings before the window closes.

Forest are in talks with Chelsea over a potential loan deal for the forward after he was made available at Stamford Bridge and not included in their opening-day squad against Fulham.

Negotiations are ongoing, but Delap fits the profile of striker Forest are prioritising and is a long-term target for both the club and Glasner from his spell at Crystal Palace.

Possession: Fulham 60%-40% ChelseaShots: 7-13Shots on target: 2-5Corners: 4-3Touches in opposition box: 16-18

An absorbing first half at Craven Cottage is brought to a close and Chelsea take a 2-1 lead into the break. Pedro put them ahead inside the first minute before King equalised for Fulham. However Rogers, on his Chelsea debut, put the visitors back in front not long before half-time.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Palmer, who has run the show for Chelsea in this first half, is inches away from putting the visitors 3-1 up. Both sides have been guilty of giving the ball away in dangerous areas and Fulham do so on this occasion. Palmer then curls an effort from the edge of the box but his shot goes just wide of the far post.

The British record transfer puts Chelsea back in front on his official debut. It stems from great play from centre-back Lacroix, who finds himself in an advanced position and receives a pass from Palmer on the right side of the box. Lacroix cuts it across to Rogers, who makes no mistake from 12 yards out. Assist and goal both coming from new signings.

A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v

Fulham fail to clear a cross from James into their box and Hato’s header falls at the feet of Lavia, whose shot from close range is saved by Leno.

Is Colwill lucky to still be on the pitch? The ball is played in behind the Chelsea defence and Colwill appeared to throw his arm across King but no foul is given. That could so easily have been given as a free-kick and a second yellow card.

Rogers drives towards the Fulham box and cuts inside onto his right foot. His effort is blocked by Cuenca before James’ first-time shot is straight at Leno.

Chelsea are inches from going back in front. It stems from great work from Palmer, who drives down Chelsea’s right. His cross from the right side of the box picks out Pedro near the penalty spot. The Brazilian volleys it first time but his effort goes just wide.

Fulham are on top at the moment and Chelsea are lucky shaky as they are under the cosh inside their own box. King is playing really well, finding pockets of space down Fulham’s right and looking a real threat.

Fulham are back on level terms but it is really poor goalkeeping from Sanchez. King, who had just threatened down Fulham’s right, receives a pass from Castagne on the right touchline and takes a touch into the Chelsea box. King then fires his shot away at the near post and gets plenty of power on it but there is no way Sanchez should be beaten. He is beaten and Fulham equalise. Good strike from King but terrible keeping from Sanchez.

Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE

Chelsea haven’t spent all that money on Rogers for his defending, but Alonso won’t have liked the way he let Josh King to run past him to collect the ball and smash Fulham level. Rogers switched off there.

King does brilliantly to drive down Fulham’s right and flashes a dangerous ball across the six-yard box but none of his teammates are on hand to meet the cross.

Fulham are flirting with danger in and around their box and are a touch fortunate not to concede a second goal.

Down the other end, King is urged to shoot from outside the box and he obliges. It looks like it should be a fairly routine save for Sanchez but the Chelsea keeper looks uncomfortable and pushes it behind for a corner. The delivery comes to the near post and King, who lays it off the edge of the box. It comes to Palacios, who cannot guide his effort on target.

Chelsea started this game well but have lost control and are asking for trouble. The latest example sees Sanchez take too long to clear and he accidentally allows the ball to go out before clearing to gift Fulham a corner. Bobb’s delivery is headed away at the near post by James.

That is strong one-vs-one defending from Bassey. Palmer lifts the ball over the top to pick out the run of Pedro, who is dispossessed inside the Fulham box by Bassey.

Moments later, Lavia flies into a reckless challenge on Bassey and is booked. Lavia looks stunned at that decision but he is perhaps on the fortunate side that VAR did not advise the referee to have a further look at that on the screen. Lavia was out of control and could have easily been in more trouble. Two Chelsea players already into the book and were a little bit lucky.

Palmer had just one Premier League assist to his name throughout last season and has already matched that tally tonight on the opening weekend.

Colwill is in trouble. Could Chelsea go down to 10 men early? He loses possession poorly inside his own half and then resorts to hacking Bobb down with a nasty challenge. Was Colwill the last man and could Bobb have gone racing in on goal? Colwill is booked and is perhaps a touch fortunate, although what saved him is that you perhaps could not definitively say that it was a denial of a goal-scoring opportunity.

How do Alvaro Arbeloa and his Fulham side react now they are a goal down early?

With their first attack of the Xabi Alonso era, Chelsea hit the front inside the opening minute of this west London derby. Lacroix’s header from halfway finds Palmer, who plays it into the path of Pedro. The Brazilian, fresh from signing a new deal at the club, takes it in his stride and, from inside the Fulham penalty area, lifts it over Leno and into the far corner. A fine finish from Pedro and Alonso has the perfect start.

"A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB

Could Joao Pedro be the man to finally lift the curse of the number nine shirt at Chelsea? Liam Delap tried and failed last season. Pedro has taken it this term and has started like a train with that early goal. Pedro has also been prolific in pre-season and has been widely tipped to be one of the Premier League’s top scorers.

Before we get going, we take a moment to remember the great Kevin Keegan, who managed Fulham in the late 1990s.

We are under way at Craven Cottage in the final game on this opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

Alvaro Arbeloa is out on the pitch for the first time in the Premier League. A friendly if not rapturous welcome from the home fans. He’s rolled his sleeves up and he’s ready to go - literally, his skinny fit jacket has sleeves rolled up tight. It looks quite uncomfortable.

It might be a new season and a new manager, but Chelsea are still doing their pre-match huddle. Fortunately, it was nowhere near the referee or the centre circle. It seemed to be captain Reece James doing all the talking.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Craven Cottage and we are moments away from kick-off in this west London derby. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up tonight:

Fulham: Leno; Castagne, Cuenca, Bassey, Robinson, King, Berge, Iwobi; Bobb, Garcia, Palacios.Substitutes: Lecomte, De Gougerolles, Tete, Reed, Charles, Sessegnon, Kevin, Smith Rowe, Muniz.

Chelsea: Sanchez; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Gusto, Lavia, James, Hato; Palmer, Pedro, Rogers.Substitutes: Penders, Chavarria, Barco, Enzo, Neto, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck, Quenda.

The boos for Fernandez from the Fulham fans got a lot louder when the players stepped on the pitch. Some people chanted something rather nasty beginning with ‘w’ as well.

There were a few boos from the Fulham fans when Enzo Fernandez’s name was read out ahead of kick-off. Clearly the England fans at Craven Cottage haven’t forgotten what happened against Argentina. Fernandez was booed by some Chelsea supporters in pre-season, but there were no loud jeers from the away end during the team announcements.

“During the week they had a few setbacks. With Moises [Caicedo], and with any [player], we do not want to take too much risk. They were not ready to play tonight. We need to go week-by-week but for tonight they were not ready.”

Chelsea certainly have an army of staff. I just counted 13 staff members helping the players through their warm-up. One of them is the new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee, who is carrying around a clipboard, presumably with all his set-piece tricks on it. Culture guru Willi Isa is also out there, as is former interim manager Calum McFarlane.

"The day to day culture that we want to build, they will play an important role" 📈Xabi Alonso explains his choice to join Chelsea and the importance of signings like Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0koZ7ZyYYx

Chelsea’s £117m man Morgan Rogers has just run out for his warm up ahead of his competitive debut for the club. He’s kept in close contact with his best mate Cole Palmer, going through a few passing drills and doing a few keepy-ups. He looks relaxed so far.

"You NEED goals if you want to win games" ⚽️New Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa speaks about the losses of Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez and the addition of Gonzalo Garcia 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/tbBujmljxm

OUTS:Andrey Santos ⇢ Manchester United, £50mMarc Cucurella ⇢ Real Madrid, £50mTyrique George ⇢ Everton, £24mAlejandro Garnacho ⇢ Aston Villa, LoanTrevoh Chalobah ⇢ Como, £30mFilip Jorgensen ⇢ Strasbourg, LoanDastan Satpaev ⇢ Burnley, LoanBenoit Badiashile ⇢ Napoli, Loan

The most interesting piece of Chelsea team news is that there is no Enzo Fernandez in the starting line-up, despite the surprise absence of Moises Caicedo. Instead, Romeo Lavia will partner Reece James in the centre of midfield, with Caicedo presumably injured. There is still an expectation that Manchester City will bid for Fernandez before the transfer window shuts, but the Argentine is on the substitutes’ bench. As expected, there is no place in the Chelsea squad for Nico Jackson and Liam Delap, both of whom have not travelled and are expected to leave Stamford Bridge. Aston Villa remain favourites to land Jackson, although Atletico Madrid have been showing an interest. Nottingham Forest are leading the race for Delap.

Alvaro Arbeloa hands full debuts to Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios, who have both joined from Real Madrid. Shea Charles is on the bench ahead of his potential Fulham debut.

Fulham: Leno; Castagne, Cuenca, Bassey, Robinson, King, Berge, Iwobi; Bobb, Garcia, Palacios.Substitutes: Lecomte, De Gougerolles, Tete, Reed, Charles, Sessegnon, Kevin, Smith Rowe, Muniz.

Morgan Rogers and Maxence Lacroix make their full Chelsea debuts this evening. Fellow new signings Danny Welbeck, Valentin Barco, Pep Chavarria and Geovany Quenda are on the bench, as is Enzo Fernandez, who has been linked with a move away. Moises Caicedo is not in the matchday squad.

Chelsea: Sanchez; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Gusto, Lavia, James, Hato; Palmer, Pedro, Rogers.Substitutes: Penders, Chavarria, Barco, Enzo, Neto, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck, Quenda.

No more excuses. No more jam tomorrow. It is time for Chelsea to fight for the Premier League title this season. Anything else should be deemed a disappointment.

This is Chelsea version 3.0 under BlueCo, who bought the club four years ago. First there was Todd Boehly’s trolley dash, then came Behdad Eghbali’s youth club. This summer the focus has been on being Premier League-ready.

Off the pitch, the timing might be right for Boehly to be discussing the sale of his shares to Eghbali’s Clearlake Capital. But on it, Chelsea look better equipped to re-enter the title conversation than at any point in the BlueCo era.

Saturday:Hull 2 Manchester United 0Everton 2 Crystal Palace 0Ipswich 2 Sunderland 1Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 1Brentford 3 Tottenham 0

Sunday:Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0Newcastle 2 Liverpool 2

Let's get it.#CFC | #FULCHE pic.twitter.com/G2M8LknNgV

Monday Night Fulham. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/Oxuni9yiez

Two former Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain teammates go head-to-head in the dugouts at Craven Cottage as Fulham host Chelsea in a west London derby to round out the opening weekend of the new Premier League season. Alvaro Arbeloa and Xabi Alonso were teammates at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain and both had stints as Real Madrid manager last season but have new homes in London. Arbeloa has replaced Marco Silva, who is now at Benfica, whilst Alonso is Liam Rosenior’s permanent replacement. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition.

“I know Alonso well because I have watched so many games of his teams,” Arbeloa said. “We have to be ready, and if we want to beat them we will have to play very well. I spoke to Xabi a few days ago. But not about football; both of our families are coming to London, and we are very good friends, until Monday night [tonight]. We will be there on the touchline, so close for 90 minutes, and we will give everything for our clubs. For those 90 minutes, we are not friends.”

Arbeloa has gone back to his former club to add a couple of players in the shape of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios. The opening weekend has not served Fulham well of late; they have won just one of their last six Premier League opening weekend fixtures. They concluded their pre-season with a 1-0 win over Stuttgart.

Chelsea have been very active in the transfer market this summer, breaking the British transfer record to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa as well as adding experience through the likes of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, whilst the likes of Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Trevoh Chalobah have moved on. They finished off their pre-season with a 3-1 victory over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge just over a week ago.

“We feel ready,” Alonso said. “We have prepared the whole pre-season with some players from the first day, other ones coming later, but the desire, the ambition, the hunger to start the Premier League is already in the building each training [session] and we are looking forward to it.”

Enzo Fernandez has been strongly linked with a move away this summer, with Manchester City’s interest well-known.

“Enzo is a Chelsea player,” Alonso added. “He is a top, top player. He is training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he is getting ready for Monday. He is training really well, good attitude and that is what we want. He is trying his best to prepare for the kick-off of the Premier League.”

These sides finished on the same number of points (52) last season, with Chelsea finishing ahead on goal difference. It was one win apiece for each club in the two Premier League meetings last season. Nearly a year ago, Chelsea won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge whilst Fulham won 2-1 in this fixture at Craven Cottage back in January. Chelsea have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage.

#1601. Sunday's Ligue 1 prediction, including Lyon vs. Brest, Rennes vs. Lille and Le Mans vs. Monaco

By Lewis Nolan | 08 Nov 2026 02:55

Today's Ligue 1 predictions involve clashes at both ends of the table, with Rennes set to welcome Lille to Roazhon Park, while hosts Monaco will clash with strugglers Le Mans at Stade Marie-Marvingt.

Elsewhere, Le Havre will face Lorient at Stade Oceane, while Angers' home clash with Nice will take place at Stade Raymond Kopa.

French giants Marseille will travel to Stade Bollaert-Delelis to take on Lens, but not before Lyon face Brest at Stade Francis-Le Ble.

Rennes welcome Lille to Roazhon Park on Sunday afternoon in round 10 of the 2026-27 Ligue 1 campaign.

In their previous league outing, Les Rouge et Noir fell to a disappointing 5-2 defeat against Nice at the Allianz Riviera, while Les Dogues snatched a late 1-0 win over Lens on home soil.

With both sides enjoying promising starts to the 2026-27 Ligue 1 campaign, Sunday’s clash is bound to be one of the highlights of the weekend and could easily go either way.

However, despite their recent struggles in the Champions League, it is extremely difficult to ignore Lille’s current surge towards the Ligue 1 summit, and we are backing them to maintain the pressure on PSG by collecting all three points this weekend.

Le Mans will hope to dig themselves out of the Ligue 1 relegation zone Sunday when they host Monaco at Stade Marie-Mavingt.

A 2-0 defeat at Troyes last week dropped MUC72 down to 17th in the table, while Monaco sit seventh after a 3-1 loss at Paris FC.

Monaco wasted many scoring chances in their last Conference League match, but should find more clear-cut opportunities against a Le Mans side that are a little over-aggressive at the back.

A new era of football at Le Havre begins on Sunday when they host Lorient at Stade Oceane on matchday 10.

The Normandy club sit bottom of the Ligue 1 table after being hammered 5-1 by Paris Saint-Germain last week, while Lorient sit 11th following a 2-0 home defeat versus Brest on Monday.

Le Havre are unlikely to face many scoring threats from Lorient, and combined with their desire to impress their new interim manager, we believe the Normandy side will finally collect maximum points.

Angers can stay above the Ligue 1 relegation line on Sunday with a victory over a rejuvenated Nice at Stade Raymond Kopa.

A 2-0 defeat at Lyon last weekend dropped Les Scoistes down to 15th in the table, while Nice climbed up to eighth after a convincing 5-2 home win versus Rennes.

Nice are starting to find their form and given how strong they are in possession we expect they will eventually wear down the home side and come out on top.

On a mission to record back-to-back wins, Brest welcome title-chasing Lyon to Stade Francis-Le Ble on Sunday afternoon for a Ligue 1 contest.

Les Pirates picked up a comfortable success at Lorient last time out, whereas Les Gones have been busy on continental duty, sharing the spoils at Real Sociedad.

After a positive result at Lorient last weekend, Brest face a tougher test in the form of Lyon this time around.

Despite exerting themselves in Spain on Thursday night, Les Gones should be fresh enough to earn a point at Stade Francis-Le Ble.

Fresh off a pulverizing Champions League defeat in midweek, Lens will try to build themselves back up when they welcome Marseille to Stade Bollaert-Delelis on Sunday.

After nine matchdays, Lens sit ninth in Ligue 1, losing 1-0 at Lille last weekend, with OM now two points above them in sixth thanks to a 2-0 win over Toulouse.

Lens may be shell-shocked when they take to the field on Sunday after that lopsided defeat in Europe this week.

As such, we expect them to play rather timidly, which will play right into Marseille's hands, who are starting to round into form, especially in this competition.

#1600. Jeff Ekhator back in Juventus group training after injury nightmare

Jeff Ekhator has finally rejoined his Juventus teammates on the training pitch. The young striker, signed from Genoa in the summer, took part in a full group session at the Continassa on Friday for the first time since a run of muscle problems that has so far kept him out of every competitive game in black and white.

His return gives Luciano Spalletti one more name to consider in a week when the squad has been kept together at the training centre ahead of Sunday’s visit of Napoli.

Juventus announced the permanent deal on 1 July, and Football Italia put the fee at €16m plus add ons. The 19 year old has barely been available since.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, who credits Sky Sport Italia with the news, his troubles began in the very first friendly of pre-season against Basel. He recovered in time to be named in the squad for the second Serie A round against Parma, where he stayed on the bench, but broke down again a few days later and has spent roughly two further months on the sidelines.

Di Marzio describes the forward as fully recovered, and Friday’s session with the rest of the group was his first since that setback.

Jeff Ekhator signs for Juventus from Genoa on a permanent deal! ⚪️⚫️ Welcome to the club, Jeff! 🙌

Nobody should expect Ekhator to be rushed into the starting eleven after so long without match practice. Football Italia sees him more as an extra option from the bench, giving Spalletti a third centre forward alongside Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani.

That alone matters for a side that has struggled for goals. Juventus have scored 11 times in nine league games, and the 2-0 defeat at Genoa on Wednesday, covered in our report on Spalletti’s apology, left them level on 14 points with Napoli.

The timing of his comeback is notable. After the Genoa loss, chief executive Giovanni Carnevali met the players and the coach, and Spalletti then decided to keep the squad together at the training ground until kick off, as explained in our piece on the Juventus retreat.

Napoli come to the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November for Matchday 10, with kick off at 20:45 local time. According to the club’s own match notes, it is the first time since April 2021 that the two sides meet on the same number of points in Serie A.

Whether Ekhator makes the matchday squad will become clear when Spalletti names his group. Either way, having a fit young striker back in training is a rare piece of good news for Juventus this week.

Sources: Gianluca Di Marzio, Football Italia, Juventus

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1599. GdS: The opportunity, the issues and the exes – why Genoa is a ‘true test’ for Amorim’s Milan

AC Milan take on Genoa this afternoon in need of a win to bounce back from a midweek defeat, which has become a familiar tale.

There is a lot riding on the game at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris for various reasons, but above all the feeling is that a positive result is required to make the international break less turbulent for Ruben Amorim and his side. La Gazzetta dello Sport have picked out a few angles in their preview.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Inter will host Como tonight: will Milan seize the day? That is the significance of the Rossoneri’s trip to Liguria. A win against Genoa would allow them to gain ground on Inter, Como, or both should the match at San Siro end in a draw.

As of this morning, Milan sit in fifth place with 21 points. If the season’s objective is a top-four finish, they must determine which team to target in the race. The top four are Lazio (28), Roma (27, having played one extra match), Inter (25) and Como (23).

Lazio is the big surprise, while the presence of the other three was to be expected. Milan won the derby, but this week’s European fixtures have re-established a gap: Inter defeated Feyenoord away in the Champions League, while Milan fell to Ferencváros at San Siro in the Europa League. Then there are Como, following their extraordinary 9-1 victory in RC Lens.

Yesterday, Roma eased past Sassuolo, ending the day in second place. Currently, Milan trail those ahead of them in the standings because – unlike the top four – they are still searching for a clear, strong identity.

Should Inter emerge victorious in Milano, a win in Genoa would allow the Diavolo to leapfrog Como and claim fourth place. So, Milan must take the opportunity, or risk further complications in their top four bid.

Inconsistency as a way of life for Milan. In their last six matches across Serie A and the Europa League, every victory has been followed by a defeat. Following this pattern of alternation, Milan should win today, having been beaten in Europe by Ferencváros on Thursday, but sequences are made to be broken.

Milan will only fully turn a corner and truly mature only when they step off this seesaw. To understand these ups and downs, one must look at the mindset. It is a psychological issue: the team do not know how to handle a win, treating it as a definitive cure only to suffer a relapse the very next time out.

Amorim is well aware of the problem: his disappointment following the Ferencváros match stemmed from the team’s attitude, which stood in stark contrast to the one displayed five days earlier against Inter. He addressed it in the dressing room (a polite way of saying he was furious).

It is unclear how much age plays a role, as Milan’s squad features a blend of youth and experience. For instance, in Thursday’s match against Ferencváros, both 20-year-old Cissé and 31-year-old Rabiot were equally ineffective.

Perhaps the question is whether there are enough figures capable of shaking up the group and keeping it alert and responsive. Judging by what is seen on the pitch, Mike Maignan possesses the strongest personality though one wonders whether his voice carries real weight.

Luka Modrić is a genius that has won it all, but he does not appear to be the type of player who rallies his team-mates, embodying instead a quiet, standard-setting form of leadership.

On Thursday, against Ferencváros, Gonçalo Ramos touched the ball 26 times over 90 minutes plus stoppage time. Among those who were not substituted, he was the least involved player for Milan.

While it is true that a centre-forward’s role naturally involves less ball possession than that of a midfielder or defender, what matters is that he remains a threat. Yet, against the Hungarians, Gonçalo was harmless, failing to register a single shot on target.

He was the Milan player who engaged in the highest number of duels (13), a statistic that reinforces the impression of a Ramos disconnected from the rest of the team, attempting to force individual solutions against multiple opponents.

So far, Ramos has appeared to be an ill-fitting piece in the side. In 13 matches across the league and the Europa League, he has scored just three goals: two in Serie A (one of which was a penalty) and one in Europe. He also has just one assist.

That is far too little for a €70m man. Gonçalo Ramos was not born a striker: he evolved into one, and he interprets the position in an atypical way, as a creative link-up player or an opportunist rather than a penalty box target man.

Much like Kolo Muani at Juventus, he functions more as a wide forward or a supplementary attacker than as an out-and-out goalscorer. There is no doubt that Gonçalo possesses refined technique, is capable of precise combination play, and excels at holding up the ball.

He started reasonably well at Milan, showing signs that he could blend flashes of brilliance with goalscoring. Gradually, however, he has faded, seemingly weighed down by a lack of confidence. It is surprising that Amorim is yet to fully unlock his qualities or integrate him effectively with the players around him.

Keep an eye on the contingent of former Milan players within the Genoa squad. Stephan El Shaarawy spent four years with the Diavolo between 2011 and 2015. Although he only won one Supercoppa Italiana, he left behind fond memories.

He is expected to start today. Daniele De Rossi has been deploying him between the left flank and the attacking midfield, where his signature drifting, inward-curving runs can pose a real threat.

Junior Messias is slated to begin on the bench, though whether that will actually be the case remains to be seen. The Brazilian spent two years in Milan, and was the standout performer in Genoa’s 2-1 victory over Lecce a week ago.

While Messias is somewhat injury-prone, he has managed to feature in every league match so far this season. Known for his creativity, he operates as a number 10 that is just as adept at setting up his team-mates as he is at scoring himself.

Lorenzo Colombo meanwhile is a product of the Milan youth academy and a favourite of Zlatan Ibrahimović, who once nicknamed him ‘Hulk’. He has seen his role in the Genoa attack diminish, as the Montenegrin player Osmajic has become the primary centre-forward.

That said, De Rossi has occasionally fielded them together to great effect. Colombo has yet to score in this Serie A campaign, though he has provided two assists, both for Osmajic.

Notably absent from the Genoa squad is the talented 18-year-old Brazilian Robinho Junior, son of the Robinho who won the 2010-11 Scudetto with Milan.

#1598. Man United could match shocking 73-year Arsenal feat in Aston Villa Premier League clash

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 07:36

Manchester United will be at risk of matching an unwanted feat last suffered by Arsenal 73 years ago when they take on Aston Villa in Sunday's Premier League finale.

The Red Devils welcome the Lions to Old Trafford after sinking to a new 40-year low, having dropped into the bottom three of the Premier League table on Saturday.

Nottingham Forest's 3-1 win over Manchester City saw the Tricky Trees leapfrog Michael Carrick's side, who are now two points adrift of safety in 18th position.

Not since 1986 have Man United found themselves in the bottom three after nine rounds of a top-flight season, and Carrick's side must win to overtake 17th-placed Coventry City on Sunday.

Should the Red Devils fail to claim all three points against Aston Villa, they would not only enter the international break in the relegation zone, but also join the worst kind of exclusive club.

Indeed, only three teams in English top-flight history have won just one of their opening 10 games of a season, after finishing in the top three of the standings the year before.

The last team to suffer that fate was Arsenal, who won just one of their first 10 matches in the 1953-54 First Division, after clinching the title in the 1952-53 campaign; the Gunners ultimately finished 12th that year.

Meanwhile, the Chelsea team of 1919-20 ranked third in the top flight, before opening the 1920-21 season with just one win from their opening 10 games en route to an 18th-placed finish.

The first - and only other club - to endure such a miserable starting run after a standout campaign the previous year was the 1894-95 Derby County side, but Man United are just 90 minutes away from entering that unwanted list.

Carrick has overseen just one win from Man Utd's first nine Premier League games in 2026-27 - alongside four draws and four losses - and the Red Devils are winless in seven top-flight clashes since thumping Ipswich Town 5-2 on August 30.

More unwanted history is on the line for the 20-time English champions on Sunday afternoon, when they could also open a season with just one win in 10 games for the first time in their Premier League history.

The Red Devils have not started a season so poorly since 1972-73, when they won one, drew four and lost five of their first 10, and only once before have they gone eight Premier League games without victory.

That occurrence happened a little over 12 months ago in April/May 2025 under Ruben Amorim, although that sequence coincidentally ended with a 2-0 win over Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

However, Carrick's men are still waiting for their first clean sheet of the Premier League season, also marking the first time in 40 years that they have gone nine games without a shut-out in a top-flight term.

#1597. Shambolic off the park, shambolic on it, dire defeat at Falkirk leaves O'Neill on thin ice

Published: 10:28 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 15:06 EDT, 3 November 2026

It took Celtic supporters the best part of half an hour on Sunday afternoon to belt out their now traditional rendition of ‘Sack the Board, Sack the Board’.

But as dysfunctional as this club may be off the park, there’s no doubt things are every bit as bad on it. This is an organisation that requires a rebuild from top to bottom. No one should be exempt.

Not the board members, not the management team, not the players. The whole thing is a shambles.

The table will show the champions are right on track to defend their crown. Indeed, the stats here will show this was a contest they dominated. But anyone with a set of eyes and any sort of common sense knows the real story.

Ahead of the match, Martin O’Neill insisted he is essentially oblivious to the outside noise around his team. Aye right.

Callum McGregor looks frustrated as Celtic go down in Falkirk

Scott Tanser celebrates his goal with Falkirk team-mate Owen Eames

Legend at the club though he may be, the Northern Irishman is surely on thin ice. Any other Celtic manager with three wins in his last 10 in all competitions certainly would be.

Frankly, he’s kidding himself on when he says he’s been satisfied with Celtic’s start to the season. The fans aren’t buying that nonsense any more. Does the man himself even believe it?

He continually talks about how his team need time to find their feet. More drivel. We’re now in November. Falkirk also signed 17 in the summer and they seem to be doing relatively well.

The football is just atrocious to watch. It has been all season. Such is the standard of the opposition in Scotland, they usually have just about enough quality to get away with it.

But that’s not a long-term solution to an increasingly worrying problem.

Falkirk, by the way, were outstanding here. They have now won four games on the bounce, each in a thoroughly un-Falkirk way.

Their success under John McGlynn has been built on the ability to pass teams off the park. This victory was far more to do with grit, determination and unity than anything else. Three qualities their opponents are lacking.

Falkirk play like a team. Celtic play like a bunch of individuals. And unless something changes pronto, things are going to get even uglier.

Just as they did in the 2-1 win over Hibernian at Easter Road last week, Celtic fell behind early doors.

Finley Barbrook picked up a loose ball midway inside the visitors’ half before finding Ryan Strain in acres of space on the right-hand side.

The full-back’s cross should have been blootered clear by Cameron Carter-Vickers at the back post with minimal fuss. Goodness knows what he actually tried to do, with the ball simply bouncing off the big American and right into the path of the grateful Ethan Ross, who couldn’t miss from five yards out.

Celtic winger Haissem Hassan gets involved in a scuffle with Falkirk players

Shocking stuff from a Celtic perspective. Carter-Vickers’ comments questioning Celtic’s ‘random’ style following defeats to Rangers in September were bang on the money. But he would do well to examine his own performances too. He’s not as good as some fans seem to think.

It took 10 minutes for Celtic to muster up a response. Liam Scales’ long ball found Camilo Duran in behind the Falkirk defence. His strike across goal from a tight angle beat Scott Bain, but not the far post.

Haissem Hassan’s curler from the follow-up was then brilliantly tipped round the post by the keeper.

Jacob Murrell is the country’s in-form striker with five goals in his last seven outings, but sclaffed a shot wide from the penalty spot at the end of a lovely move involving Owen Eames and Scott Tanser down at the corner flag.

Duran should have levelled things up on the half-hour mark after getting on the end of a wicked Hassan ball into the six-yard box, but headed straight at Bain. Anywhere else but right down the middle would have done the trick.

He was made to pay for that miss as Falkirk doubled their advantage with a wonderful team goal on 38 minutes. Eames was given far too much space on the Falkirk left, but take nothing away from the way he threaded an inch-perfect pass into the path of the underlapping Tanser.

He took one touch to set himself as he drove into the box before coolly slotting past Johnstone. It was the kind of football we’ve become accustomed to seeing on a weekly basis from this side under John McGlynn.

Yes, Celtic looked like they couldn’t even be bothered to try and stop them but that’s not Falkirk’s problem. Their execution was flawless.

Man-of-the-Match Bain was once again called into action as the break came into view, and he once again stepped up, tipping Duran’s left-footed strike from 18 yards around the post.

Martin O'Neill looks on in dismay as Celtic suffer in Falkirk

O’Neill could have taken off any one of his so-called big-name stars at half-time and there would have been no grounds for complaint. He settled for just the one, replacing Callum Osmand with James Forrest.

Osmand should never be playing on the wing anyway. In Yang Hyun-Jun’s absence – and with Jota still searching for fitness – he has had a run of games in that position. You suspect he won’t be holding on to it for long. Square pegs in round holes, and all that.

If O’Neill did give his players a boot up the backside at the interval, you wouldn’t have known it, conceding a shocking third through Murrell within minutes of the restart. Fortunately for the visitors, they got away with it, with VAR spotting that the ball was bundled in by the striker’s hand.

Forrest forced a comfortable stop from Bain on the half-turn, with Callum McGregor then blazing over from a promising position.

The captain has been a shadow of himself all season. In truth, he looks a yard or two off the pace.

For so long, we’ve heard that Celtic just can’t do without him. However, playing like this, he isn’t helping this team.

Bain’s stop to deny Forrest on 68 minutes was simple enough. The one which denied substitute Benjamin Nygren seconds later to seal the points was right out of the top drawer.

The Bairns hadn’t beaten Celtic in 19 years coming into this one. Given the state of this Celtic side, is anyone truly surprised that run has come to a halt?

#1596. Crystal Palace vs. Liverpool: Andoni Iraola could match Sir Alex Ferguson, Jose Mourinho in Premier League fixture

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 07:58, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 08:03

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola could match a terrific Sir Alex Ferguson and Jose Mourinho record in Sunday's Premier League battle with Crystal Palace.

The Reds head to Selhurst Park looking to avoid a third straight defeat in all tournaments, having gone down to Arsenal and Fenerbahce already this month.

Iraola oversaw five straight victories before his two recent setbacks, and he has been warned that he faces unwanted Arne Slot comparisons if he fails to lead Liverpool to victory in the capital.

However, the former Bournemouth boss has overseen an extraordinary run of away matches both with the Cherries and the Reds, who are still unbeaten on the road in the 2026-27 Premier League.

Liverpool have won three and drawn one of their four top-flight away games, while Iraola is incredibly unbeaten in Premier League away matches throughout the entirety of 2026.

The Spaniard has not lost a top-flight contest on the road since December 2025, when his Bournemouth side were slain by Brentford, and he has since gone 13 without defeat on rival territory.

Should Liverpool take at least a point home from Selhurst Park, Iraola would equal the away unbeaten runs of Alex Ferguson (14 in 1999), Jose Mourinho (14 in 2005) in Premier League road matches in a single calendar year.

However, Iraola would not match the outright record for consecutive Premier League away games without defeat in one calendar year, as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's Manchester United avoided losing in 15 successive top-flight road matches in 2021.

After opening the campaign with a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United, Liverpool have won their last three Premier League matches outside Anfield, overcoming Ipswich Town, Bournemouth and nine-man Brentford.

It has been over two years since Liverpool won more Premier League away games in a row, as Slot's 2024-25 team prevailed in each of their first four, the fourth of which came at none other than Palace.

While Iraola could match Ferguson and Mourinho with a desired outcome, defeat would see Liverpool suffer an unwanted club first in the Premier League era.

The then-reigning champions were beaten 2-1 by Crystal Palace in September 2025, when Eddie Nketiah struck a 97th-minute winner after earlier strikes from Ismaila Sarr and Federico Chiesa.

Defeat on Sunday would therefore see Liverpool lose back-to-back games away to Crystal Palace for the first time in the Premier League, having not suffered that fate since the First Division days of 1992.

The Reds start the day sixth in the Premier League table, one point below Everton and Chelsea, whom they can overtake with a win if the Blues fail to beat rock-bottom Sunderland.

Juventus and Napoli go into Sunday’s Serie A Matchday 10 meeting at the Allianz Stadium level on points. Both benches will look different. Napoli will be without their head coach, with assistant Landucci on the bench. Spalletti is still missing seven players.

Allegri was sent off in Napoli’s 3-3 home draw with Roma. Serie A’s sporting judge then punished him for disrespectful remarks to the match officials. The ban covered the trip to Monza on 28 October and now the visit to Juventus. Napoli first announced an appeal. Allegri dropped it, saying he feared the ban could rise to four matches. The suspension is now final.

Napoli also lost Lobotka at Monza. He was stretchered off just after the 15th minute following a challenge with Mangas. The club’s medical update found damage to the tibiofibular syndesmosis in his left ankle, without instability. He also has a low-grade injury to the anterior talofibular ligament. #1593. Man City star Phil Foden admits he may not have done enough to regain his place in Thomas Tuchel's England squad this week - despite being 'really happy' with his upturn in form

Published: 15:13 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 15:35 EDT, 3 November 2026

Phil Foden believes that he is approaching somewhere close to his best but remains unsure whether that is enough to earn an England recall this week.

The Manchester City midfielder missed out on the World Cup squad and was also overlooked for the lengthy four-game September camp, having last featured for his country in March.

Foden has four goals in his previous five appearances for City ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League trip to RB Leipzig in a most encouraging spell for almost 12 months. Thomas Tuchel will announce his next squad for Nations League ties with Croatia and Spain on Friday morning.

‘I haven't really spoken to him to be honest,’ Foden said when asked if he’d held talks with Tuchel in light of improving performances.

‘Football's full of ups and downs and it's one of the things you can't control. You just have to keep putting in performances. Hopefully one day the call-up might come.’

All of Jude Bellingham, Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer, Eberechi Eze and Morgan Gibbs-White have been ahead of Foden in Tuchel’s pecking order at various points across the year.

Phil Foden thinks he is finding close to his best form again at Manchester City

Foden was sent off during the derby victory at Manchester United in September and did not play for over a month. The 26-year-old went on holiday to recharge and despite not being given a true run of starts in the Premier League, is feeling consistency returning to his game.

‘I think personally this season has gone really well,’ he added. ‘Obviously I had the unfortunate red card against United, but the break did me good. I think I came back really fresh in my mind and sharp. I've been involved in a lot of goals recently, so I've been really happy.’

City boss Enzo Maresca admitted in the summer that it is his duty to enliven Foden after two disappointing seasons and is directly pitting him against Rayan Cherki for the No 10 spot.

‘I see Phil day by day better and better for sure, 100 per cent,’ Maresca said. ‘He is going to give us many things this season.

‘We have many games in all competitions and 20 senior players, all of them very good. It's good to have competition between them. Phil and Rayan are more or less in the same position. I'm very happy in the way Phil is working every day.’

Leipzig coach Martin Demichelis, meanwhile, is relishing a reunion with Maresca.

Demichelis, a former City defender, played alongside the City boss at Malaga.

'We know each other very well and we’re almost like brothers,' said former Argentina international Demichelis.

'I know his philosophy and how he wants to play. Enzo is a winner and he’ll be looking to win trophies with Manchester City.'

Foden says he has 'not really' spoken to England boss Thomas Tuchel recently

Demichelis was part of the side that won the Premier League in 2014 and also featured in two League Cup triumphs.

'I had three fantastic years at Manchester City myself, but that was a long time ago,' he said. 'Being a coach is a completely different job.'

Demichelis took charge at Leipzig in the summer after previous spells at River Plate, Monterrey and Mallorca.

They are fourth in the Bundesliga, three points behind leaders Bayern Munich after a 2-0 win at Schalke on Saturday.

Their Champions League campaign has been less convincing, with 4-1 defeats to Como and Real Madrid either side of a 1-0 victory over PSV Eindhoven.

Demichelis said: 'The players needed time to get to know me, and I needed time to get to know them but we’ve played well in our last three games.'

#1591. Fermin Lopez matches Diego Maradona's Barcelona goal tally

By Naim Beneddra | 08 Nov 2026 08:18

Barcelona midfielder Fermin Lopez has matched Diego Maradona's official goals tally for the Catalan giants, reaching a remarkable milestone while revealing how Hansi Flick has helped transform his game.

The 23-year-old has now scored 38 goals in 150 competitive appearances for Barcelona, equalling the total registered by the legendary Argentine during his two seasons at Camp Nou between 1982 and 1984.

Fermin has also contributed 36 assists since breaking into the first team under Xavi Hernandez, taking his overall tally to 74 direct goal involvements despite operating primarily as an attacking midfielder.

In an exclusive interview with Mundo Deportivo, the Spain international reflected on the comparison with Maradona and explained why he has become increasingly effective in the final third.

His comments come ahead of Barcelona's La Liga showdown with Atletico Madrid on Sunday, when he could reach another landmark by making his 100th appearance in the Spanish top flight.

Maradona's time at Barcelona was relatively brief, lasting just two seasons before his move to Napoli in 1984.

The Argentina icon scored 38 goals in 58 official appearances for the club, a considerably higher scoring rate than Fermin's 38 in 150 matches.

Nevertheless, matching the total of one of football's greatest players represents a notable achievement for a midfielder who was still struggling to establish himself in Barcelona's academy only a few years ago.

Asked about reaching Maradona's tally, Fermin was careful not to exaggerate the significance of the comparison.

"At the end of the day, they're just numbers. I can't compare myself to a player like Maradona, and everyone has their own path," he told Mundo Deportivo.

"But I'm also very happy to have matched the goal tally of a player like him. Hopefully, there will be many more."

Fermin's attacking contribution has been particularly impressive since the start of the current campaign.

He has registered six goals and seven assists this season, becoming an increasingly influential figure in Flick's midfield.

According to figures discussed during the interview, the Spaniard has averaged a goal or assist every 108 minutes since making his senior debut, with that rate improving to one direct contribution every 72 minutes this term.

The midfielder believes his ability to attack space and arrive in goalscoring positions has always been a natural part of his game.

"My main quality is that I'm a very direct player," he explained.

"Ever since I was little, I've had that mentality of always moving forward, towards goal, thinking about scoring and creating chances."

Although he has become an accomplished provider for his teammates, Fermin admitted that finding the net himself remains his preferred contribution.

His first-team breakthrough came in August 2023 under Xavi, following a productive loan spell at Linares Deportivo, where he scored 12 goals.

He subsequently struck 11 times in his debut senior campaign at Barcelona, establishing the foundations for the attacking output he has maintained under Flick.

While Fermin credits Xavi with giving him the confidence to express himself at senior level, he believes Flick has been instrumental in improving his decision-making.

The German manager has encouraged the midfielder to recognise when to accelerate attacks and when a more measured approach is required.

"I think I've improved a lot in terms of maturity under Hansi," Fermin said.

"Before, I was perhaps going at full speed all the time, rushing things a bit. With Flick, I've learned to read situations better, to understand matches and know when to do something and when not to."

That development has helped the 23-year-old become more efficient without sacrificing the aggressive movement that makes him dangerous around the penalty area.

Fermin explained that he now feels calmer when deciding whether to shoot, pass or make a run beyond the opposition's defensive line.

He also acknowledged that working closely with Flick and analysing individual situations has helped him improve the timing of his arrivals in the box.

His progress has come despite competition for attacking midfield positions, particularly from fellow Spain international Dani Olmo.

However, Fermin rejected any suggestion of tension between the pair, describing their rivalry for places as healthy and beneficial to both players.

The midfielder's immediate attention now turns to Sunday's visit to Atletico Madrid, where Barcelona will attempt to protect their two-point advantage over Diego Simeone's side at the top of La Liga.

Fermin is also set to reach 100 league appearances if selected, adding another personal milestone to an increasingly productive spell at the club.

Having already drawn level with Maradona's official Barcelona goal total, his next goal would take him beyond the Argentine's tally, although the two players' very different roles and appearance records make any broader comparison inappropriate.

#1590. Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

“For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

“We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”

Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

Cardiff City vs NorwichDoncaster Rovers vs MiddlesbroughBarnsley vs Crewe AlexandraBlackburn Rovers vs Sheffield UnitedBlackpool vs Lincoln CityCambridge United vs MillwallFleetwood Town vs Shrewsbury TownIpswich Town vs Leicester CityPlymouth vs Coventry CitySheffield Wednesday vs Wolverhampton WanderersSouthampton vs West Ham United Stevenage Town vs ReadingStoke City vs Hull City Walsall vs Leyton OrientWatford Peterborough UnitedBirmingham City vs BrentfordNottingham Forest vs Leeds United

The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”

Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood

Subs Victor, Murillo, Abbott, Netz, Hutchinson, Ndoye, McAtee, Sangare, Hudson Odoi

Leeds United Trafford; Rodon, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Ampadu, Tanaka, Longstaff, Justin; James, Okafor; Nmecha

Subs Perri, Lienou, Bijol, Bogle, Wilson, Cresswell, Stach, Aaronson, Calvert-Lewin

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi

Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

#1588. Celtic boss Martin O'Neill and board given 'hard but fair' grilling by fans in Greenock

Published: 15:16 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EDT, 3 November 2026

Martin O’Neill and senior Celtic board members were subjected to ‘hard but fair’ questioning in a meeting at Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club on Monday night, the club have revealed.

The manager was joined by chairman Brian Wilson, chief executive Michael Nicholson, chief financial officer Chris McKay and other club officials for a two-and-a-half-hour question-and-answer session that revolved around recruitment, transfer policy, communications and the club’s ambitions and strategy.

Representatives from Greenock, Port Glasgow, Gourock, Johnny Doyle, Port Glasgow Hibs and Largs supporters clubs were among around 120 Celtic fans who attended ‘to seek information and voice concerns’.

Martin O'Neill and the Celtic board met supporters in Greenock

The meeting came just a day after Celtic’s 2-0 defeat at Falkirk left them with just three wins from their past 10 matches in all competitions.

O’Neill, whose own position has come under intense scrutiny recently, told the Hoops’ website: ‘I asked to attend the meeting because I want to meet supporters as much as I possibly can.

‘We have had a few difficult weeks in recent times and I understand our supporters’ frustrations, but my resolve and the commitment of the players is as strong as ever to continue to bring success and progress to the club.’

Wilson vowed that the club would take on board concerns raised by supporters.

‘We were grateful to the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club for hosting this event in a way that allowed everyone to make their points, many of them critical, and to ask questions which we did our best to answer,’ the chairman said. ‘We didn’t expect an easy ride and didn’t get one, but the meeting was conducted in a constructive and mutually respectful way and the messages delivered by supporters will be taken on board and learned from.’
