#1587. Man United transfer news: £8.4m left-back 'sensation' on Jason Wilcox shortlist for January

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 08:23

Manchester United have reportedly identified 21-year-old Rennes starlet Mahamadou Nagida as a new left-back target following a series of encouraging scouting reports.

The Red Devils are expected to pursue a new left-sided defender as a matter of priority in 2027 and have been linked with as many as 12 left-backs ahead of the January window.

The long-serving Luke Shaw was a stalwart in that position during the 2025-26 season, starting every single Premier League game, but the Englishman's fitness problems have returned in 2026-27.

Shaw has been limited to five appearances in all competitions, while Patrick Dorgu has played just one more game due to injuries of his own.

Michael Carrick has also shown little faith in 19-year-old Harry Amass, who is yet to make a Premier League appearance this term, instead favouring Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui as emergency left-backs.

Now, TEAMTalk claims that Rennes' Nagida has emerged as a new option for Man United sporting director Jason Wilcox, whose team have been 'intensively scouting' the 2005-born defender throughout the campaign.

A product of the Rennes youth system, Nagida has scored one goal and set up two more in 13 games this season, and he was also part of the Cameroon squad at the last Africa Cup of Nations.

Man United scouts were supposedly in attendance to watch the defender during Rennes' recent Europa League games against Olympiacos and Juventus, in which Nagida played the full 90 in both games and helped Les Rouges et Noir keep a clean sheet against the former.

Already labelled a 'sensation' at his tender age, Nagida's scouting reports have been 'extremely positive', and he is only valued at €10m (£8.4m) by Transfermarkt.

However, Rennes are in a strong position to demand a lot more for the Cameroon international, who is under contract at Roazhon Park until 2029, having signed an extension last September.

Nagida is just one of a plethora of left-backs linked with moves to Old Trafford in recent times, a list that also includes out-of-favour Barcelona man Alejandro Balde.

Man United have received a boost in their efforts to sign the Spaniard, who is under no illusions that he may have to leave Camp Nou to reignite his career at the top level, having played just 124 minutes this season.

A shock move for Manchester City's Rayan Ait-Nouri is supposedly in the works too, and a breakthrough is said to have been reached in their pursuit of the Algerian.

RB Leipzig's David Raum and Newcastle United's Lewis Hall are two more prime targets for Man United, who could match an unwanted 73-year Arsenal feat in Sunday's Premier League battle with Aston Villa.

#1586. Alajbegović’s first Serie A goal and Boga sink ten-man Napoli on Juventus’s birthday

Juventus beat Napoli 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium, with both goals arriving after a goalless first half. Luciano Spalletti's side now sit seventh, with Napoli eighth, ahead of a Europa League trip to AZ Alkmaar.

A first Serie A goal from a Bosnian teenager and a late curler from a substitute gave Juventus victory over Napoli on Sunday 1 November 2026. The game at the Allianz Stadium was goalless at half-time. It finished 2-0.

The result followed a difficult run. Juventus had won just one of their previous four Serie A games. Their last outing ended in a 0-2 defeat against Genoa. Some home fans jeered the team early in the second half.

Napoli’s own match report described the first hour as balanced, with good chances for both teams, before Juventus took control. Guglielmo Vicario made an excellent early save to keep out a diving header from Lorenzo Lucca. Juan Cabal hit the post before the half-hour mark.

Spalletti changed the game from the bench. Federico Gatti replaced Weston McKennie at the break. Edon Zhegrova came on for Randal Kolo Muani on 59 minutes. The substitute skipped past Rrahmani and laid the ball off to Alajbegović. Alajbegović cut inside and fired a left-footed shot into the far corner beyond Alex Meret.

Napoli were then reduced to ten men. Kelly and Jérémie Boga had replaced Jhon Lucumí and Alajbegović on 72 minutes. Andrea Cambiaso came on for Cabal on 83. He set up Boga, who sealed the win with a right-footed curler three minutes from time.

Sky Sport Italia’s ratings made Alajbegović man of the match and called the win important for keeping Juventus in the race for the European places. Across the full 90 minutes, the match statistics favoured the home side. Juventus had 18 shots to Napoli’s 8, with 4 on target against 1. They also won 13 corners to 4. Possession was almost level, at 49% to 51%.

After ten games, Spalletti’s side have five wins, two draws and three defeats. Lazio lead the table on 28 points after nine wins and a draw.

Primo gol in carriera in Serie A, così. ✨ pic.twitter.com/TTGoL4MMyR

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 1, 2026

It was a second straight league win over Napoli for Juventus, who beat them 3-0 on 25 January 2026. Napoli’s defeat ended a run that included a 4-1 win over Monza. They now face FC Porto away in the Champions League on Wednesday 4 November.

Juventus travel to AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League League Phase on Thursday 5 November, with kick-off at 21:00 CET.

#1584. Pocognoli backs returning star McTominay to lead Scotland into new era

Published: 15:09 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 15:55 EDT, 3 November 2026

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli has welcomed Scott McTominay back into the fold after heart surgery and revealed he’s banking on him to help kickstart a new era for the national team.

McTominay went through a minor operation to address mild benign arrhythmia in September and missed Pocognoli’s first Nations League camp as head coach.

However, having scored four times after returning to action at Italian outfit Napoli, the 29-year-old midfielder is back in the squad for this month’s double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

Torino striker Che Adams, absent last time out due to a muscle strain, is also back in the fold while there is a first call-up for left-back James Penrice, currently on loan at Rangers from Greek side AEK Athens.

Celtic left-back Kieran Tierney returns after withdrawing from Pocognoli’s first squad while centre-back Scott McKenna misses out after reportedly picking up a back strain playing for Dinamo Zagreb. Josh Doig, Colby Donovan, James Wilson and Lennon Miller also drop out from Pocognoli’s debut matches.

Scott McTominay is fit and available for Scotland after minor heart surgery

Speaking while naming his squad at Hampden Park, Pocognoli emphasised the role McTominay will play – along with other senior stars – in helping bring through a new generation of stars under his guidance.

‘I have been in contact with Scott from the first day. He missed the first camp with some physical problem,’ stated the Belgian.

‘We were still in contact during the rehabilitation, when he came back on the pitch. He’s one of the captains, so there’s a special contact with them, but he’s looking forward to come, to play for us, to play in a different way, on the pitch and he is very positive, so that’s important.

‘There is plenty of experience back in the squad. With Scott, with Che, with Kieran. He’s also back, so, if you accumulate the caps, we have some experience that will be useful for this camp and to also embrace the young lads - because we still have a young squad with many players who don’t have a lot of caps.

‘I’m sure the mix will be good and these (experienced) players will also show the way for them.’

Sebastien Pocognoli has picked his squad to face North Macedonia and Switzerland

Scotland are third in Group B1 with four points from four games, three points behind Slovenia and eight behind runaway leaders Switzerland. The Scots host North Macedonia at Hampden on November 13 with a trip to Switzerland three days later.

With one eye on the forthcoming 2028 European Championship qualifying campaign, Pocognoli said: ‘I’m looking forward to working with everybody, but, for sure, we want to see most of the players just to have as much information as possible to start the qualification for the Euros.

‘All I want to do now is to get the most out of this, to know my squad as deeply as possible, to see the body language, the attitude of the players in some situations, and to have most of the information to start the big job.’

On the issue of a first call-up for 27-year-old former Hearts defender Penrice, Pocognoli said: ‘Like I said in the first camp, we have a list of players that we select regarding the performance at their clubs, but also the style of play or the way that we want to play.

‘We have some missing players around the left side, so, combined with his quality and what we are looking for on the pitch, it’s a logical choice for me. It can be very useful for the system that we want to play and also I think he deserves it.’

#1583. Kylian Mbappe extends Real Madrid scoring streak to seven games

By Naim Beneddra | 08 Nov 2026 09:19

Kylian Mbappe has extended his remarkable goalscoring streak to seven consecutive matches, helping Real Madrid move level on points with Barcelona at the top of La Liga following Saturday's 3-0 victory over Valencia.

The France international scored Madrid's third goal at Mestalla, taking his tally to 17 goals in just 16 appearances across all competitions this season.

Mbappe has now found the net in each of his last seven outings for Jose Mourinho's side, maintaining a scoring run that has become increasingly important during Madrid's recent resurgence.

The victory also extended Los Blancos' winning sequence to eight matches across La Liga and the Champions League, leaving them on 30 points alongside Barcelona, who retain first place on goal difference.

With Hansi Flick's side preparing to face third-placed Atletico Madrid on Sunday evening, Mbappe's latest contribution has increased the pressure on Madrid's title rivals.

➕3️⃣ ¡Nos volvemos a Madrid con los tres puntos! @Emirates https://t.co/fiECHdUsNJ

Mbappe's goal against Valencia arrived in the 75th minute, after the Frenchman had been frustrated by several opportunities earlier in the second half.

Arda Guler provided the decisive pass, producing an excellent turn before releasing his teammate into the penalty area.

Mbappe took the ball past goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski and finished to complete Madrid's 3-0 victory.

It was his 13th goal in 12 La Liga appearances this season, with another four strikes coming in the Champions League.

The 27-year-old's latest achievement puts him in distinguished company among Real Madrid's most prolific forwards.

According to figures highlighted by Spanish statistician Alexis Martin-Tamayo, better known as MisterChip, both Cristiano Ronaldo and Karim Benzema enjoyed seven-match scoring runs during their careers at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Ronaldo achieved the feat on several occasions, including longer sequences of 10 and 12 consecutive appearances with a goal.

The Portuguese superstar's 12-match runs, recorded in 2014 and 2018, underline the exceptional consistency required to maintain such a sequence over an extended period.

Benzema also scored in seven successive matches during spells in 2021 and 2022.

Mbappe has previously surpassed his current streak, having found the net in eight consecutive Real Madrid appearances during 2025.

His latest run is therefore not a personal record, but it provides another indication of the consistency he has established in Mourinho's attack.

The Frenchman has been particularly influential during a period in which Madrid have continued winning despite the absence of Vinicius Junior, who completed his four-match La Liga suspension against Valencia.

Mbappe also played a part in the opening goal at Mestalla, with Federico Valverde converting the rebound after his free kick struck the defensive wall.

Valverde's 28th-minute strike was followed eight minutes later by Guler's close-range finish from a Jude Bellingham delivery.

Although Madrid had established a comfortable advantage by half time, Mbappe continued searching for his goal.

Dimitrievski denied him twice after the interval before the Frenchman's persistence was eventually rewarded.

Valencia captain Jose Gaya was subsequently sent off for fouling Mbappe as he threatened to break clear, completing a difficult evening for the hosts.

Madrid's success at Mestalla was their eighth consecutive victory in all competitions, a run that has strengthened their position after a difficult spell earlier in the season.

Mourinho's team have recovered from their derby defeat against Atletico Madrid and have since recorded victories in both domestic and European competition.

The result against Valencia was also their tenth La Liga win of the campaign, taking them to 30 points from 12 matches.

Barcelona have the same total from 11 games, meaning the Catalan side remain in control of their position at the summit.

However, Sunday's encounter at the Metropolitano presents a significant challenge for Flick's team.

Atletico begin the match just two points behind Barcelona and Madrid, with a victory potentially taking Diego Simeone's side above both rivals.

The result will therefore determine whether Madrid enter the November international break level with the leaders, narrowly behind them or facing a renewed deficit.

For Mourinho, the immediate concern will be maintaining his team's momentum when club football resumes later this month.

Madrid are scheduled to host Celta Vigo on November 21, when Vinicius will once again be available following his suspension.

His return will give Mourinho additional attacking options, particularly with Guler and Yan Diomande having impressed during the Brazilian's absence.

Mbappe, meanwhile, has made his own position at the heart of Madrid's attack increasingly difficult to question.

With 17 goals already this season and a scoring streak stretching across seven appearances, the Frenchman is providing the finishing touch to a team that has rediscovered its winning rhythm.

#1582. Liverpool backed to copy Arsenal against Crystal Palace after "unforgivable" Fenerbahce defeat

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 09:34

Ahead of Sunday's Premier League clash between Crystal Palace and Liverpool at Selhurst Park, Sports Mole site coordinator Ben Knapton explains why he expects the Reds to follow in Arsenal's footsteps and produce a massive response to their "pathetic" and "unforgivable" Champions League defeat to Fenerbahce.

This reminds me of what I said after Fleetwood against Arsenal: I expected a massive response from Arsenal at Liverpool, which is what Arteta got. I am expecting a similarly big response from Liverpool in this one.

The two defeats were very different; the Arsenal defeat was different in the sense that Liverpool were quite well organised for a lot of that game, but got done by an Alisson mistake giving the ball away.

Then against Fenerbahce, it was at the other end of the pitch where it was absolutely embarrassing, pathetic, calamitous. All three goals were so preventable and unforgivable.

It was the first time they had taken a lead and lost under Iraola. Also the first time scoring in a game and losing under Iraola, and the latest they have ever taken a lead in a European game and still lost.

The players could easily be accused of switching off and wilting in the cauldron of the Turkish atmosphere, which as many teams know when facing Turkish teams away from home is an atmosphere like none other.

Liverpool have had a bit of a perpetual problem with Turkish atmospheres; they lost twice to Galatasaray last season. Maybe there is some sort of psychological thing going on there for Liverpool.

But they are playing in the English capital this week, not in Turkey, and that is already a boost.

Losing Gravenberch for that Fenerbahce game did not help. Nyoni in midfield, in my view, was very fortunate to escape at least a yellow card in the first few minutes against Arsenal. But the fans have really taken to him, and he was one of the few who could hold his head high after the Fenerbahce game.

Liverpool have got 10 points from their four Premier League away games this season, so I am expecting a massive response.

They will be facing an out-of-form Crystal Palace, a tired Crystal Palace, a defensively disorganised Crystal Palace. I have complete faith in Liverpool to get the response Iraola will be demanding.

#1581. Mikel Arteta reveals Arsenal have a 'massive library' of videos showing rivals pulling shirts - as he hits back after Alexander Isak controversy

Published: 15:50 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 16:22 EDT, 3 November 2026

Mikel Arteta has revealed he has a ‘massive library’ of video footage showing other teams pulling shirts - having last month disclosed he is keeping a similar dossier of other Premier League managers leaving their technical area.

Arsenal defender Jurrien Timber escaped punishment for making contact with Alexander Isak in Arsenal’s 1-0 victory over Liverpool on Sunday.

Timber tugged Isak’s shirt as the striker went to head the ball towards goal, but referee Andy Madley did not award a foul and VAR decided against recommending an on-field review. The decision has since been widely scrutinised.

When asked if there is now a danger referees will change tack and give penalties for and free-kicks for the offence, Arteta said: ‘Yeah, I have a lot of clips about shirt pulls and grabs.

‘I have a massive library that we can talk about. I have a massive library that we can (put out) there to remind everybody what every team is going through.’

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola and captain Virgil van Dijk were outraged when they weren't awarded a penalty after Jurrien Timber pulled back Alexander Isak

Now Mikel Arteta has claimed he is keeping a dossier of similar incidents of shirt pulling which has gone unpunished

Last month Arteta claimed his touchline behaviour is punished far more harshly than that of other Premier League managers and said he had clips of his counterparts breaching their own technical areas as evidence.

‘I do have to be careful, and we need to have good sensors there,’ Arteta said after being booked during Arsenal's 2-0 win over Everton.

‘There are managers that have the record in the league - 36 times in 10 minutes leaving the touchline, no yellows.

‘So I'm clipping all of that. I have a massive storage of images. So if somebody is going to say, “I'm not in the record yet, somebody else has the record”, then it's 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the (other) manager.

Arteta also revealed William Saliba is ready to make his first appearance since sustaining a back injury in July as he pushes to feature against Slavia Prague on Wednesday.

Saliba played 45 minutes in behind-closed-doors friendly last week and was part of Arsenal’s travelling squad for their Champions League fixture in Prague.

The 25-year-old also took part in full training this morning for the first time since picking up a back injury in France's World Cup semi-final loss to Spain in July.

Arsenal have coped well without him, with summer signing Ezri Konsa forming an impressive partnership with Gabriel. The Gunners have conceded only five goals in nine Premier League games, which is the best defensive record in the division.

William Saliba is back in contention for the Gunners after missing the start of the season with a back injury sustained at the World Cup

Arteta said: ‘He's in a really good place. I think the timings and the manner that the injury has been dealt with, and especially the feelings that Willy has been having along the way, have been very, very positive.

‘He feels very comfortable, he played 45 minutes behind closed doors last week and he feels ready to go. So whether we use him or not now is a matter of what the team needs.

‘All the preparation has been done to measure all the loads and minimise the risk. Now he's in a really good place, he's built the capacity that we needed and now it's about giving him minutes.’

On how eager Saliba is to play, he added: ‘I think he's very desperate and very loved, because William is somebody that is admired and very liked around the team.

‘Every time he's around, he creates something special. That's William, that's his nature. He's around the team now, and we need to give him the right moment, the right amount of minutes, and hopefully that's going to be very soon.’
